comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Closed by the freeze of `trials/e1-checked/protocol.md` and `trials/e1-checked/tasks.md` (2026-10-31).

Acceptance check (named observation):
- 30 held-out tasks frozen in tasks.md (A1-A10 core language, B1-B10 authority and I/O, C1-C10 concurrency, parallelism, contracts), none reused from earlier trials or docs; close models disclosed in protocol §2.
- Paired Tide/Rust protocol with D0's thresholds unchanged (protocol §8: F(Tide) >= 0.8 F(Rust), P(Tide) >= P(Rust), I(Tide) <= 1.5 I(Rust)).
- Exact executable prerequisites in protocol §10.1, each owned by a bead that blocks fx-ic2: fx-kw8.9, fx-nkv.1-6, and the fourteen new e1-prereq beads fx-zc1, fx-o8j, fx-ugm, fx-o4h, fx-iob, fx-byk, fx-5vj, fx-hxw, fx-3iu, fx-08m, fx-mhd, fx-m72, fx-yg5, fx-u65 (`br dep tree fx-ic2`).
- A metadata-only pilot (protocol §9) cannot report E1 as passed or failed; neither can a gate run missing any readiness item (§1, §10.2).

Technical decisions (AGENTS.md Decisions), with reasons:
1. Sample: two independent fresh writers per task per arm (60 trials per arm). One per task leaves the P(Tide) >= P(Rust) comparison at the mercy of a single trial; more costs writer sessions without changing the gate's point-estimate form.
2. One fresh session per task, not one writer doing all tasks: no carry-over learning or order effects between tasks.
3. Rust arm may use serde, serde_json, thiserror (pinned 1.0.229 / 1.0.154 / 2.0.21): exactly the crates whose behavior Tide builds in (derive(Error), Encode/Decode), so paired tasks ask the same work of both arms.
4. Rand, Net::get/HTTP, Proc, simulated crashes left out (protocol §11): Rust's std cannot express a paired task without handing that arm extra code.
5. Checked cases are visible to writers and the grader's suites implement exactly them: grading stays mechanical and identical in both arms; held-out means held out from the reference and earlier trials, not hidden from the writer.
6. First check also compiles the acceptance suite for libraries, so a skeleton first run cannot pass.
7. Iterations: mean runs over trials that pass final (D0's "iterations to green"); counting failures as the cap diluted the 1.5x ratio (r1 Opus finding 1). The censored mean is reported as information.
8. Concurrency that no checked case can witness (C1-C6, C9) is checked by a recorded, line-cited grader review; text-search structure checks alone do not prove it (r1 Codex 5, r2 Opus 1).
9. fx-u65 (every FX code the reference names) is a prerequisite: without it a Tide writer can pass with code the reference forbids, which flatters Tide (r1 Codex 2).
10. Writer code runs only in a harness OS sandbox with a read allowlist (protocol §10.3): fx-kw8.9's build mode is for reviewed code, and the sandbox must keep suites and reference solutions unreadable.

Reviews (reviews/fx-gfq-r<N>-<reviewer>.md): r1 Opus and Codex on frozen candidate d1bd3f2c (both request_changes), r2 Opus (2 text fixes), r3 Opus approve, r4 Codex narrow re-check (lint severity), r5 Opus+Codex narrow (FX0510 is v1), r6 Opus+Codex narrow approve on final diff e37f7903 (taken before the review files were added).

Not taken (non-blocking, recorded for fx-ic2): an unblocked bead that builds the harness, suites, and reference solutions early to surface prerequisite gaps sooner; narrowing fx-u65 to the FX codes a single-file package can reach (that would loosen readiness item 3 and is the owner's call).

title: Define the Ferox ownership model so it preserves Rust-grade safe-code guarantees through a smaller and more restrictive mechanism
description: Synthesize the Ferox ownership model from the now-separated subproblems: guarantee boundary/invariants and concrete ownership/borrowing rules. This bead should consolidate those decisions into one coherent ownership proposal that the rest of the language can depend on.
design:
Primary question: Given the guarantee boundary and the concrete ownership/borrowing rules, what is the final integrated Ferox ownership model?

This synthesis task should:
1. Reconcile the invariant-level commitments with the rule-level design.
2. Surface any tension between simplicity, usability, and soundness.
3. Produce the final ownership model that downstream concurrency, source-language, and verification beads can treat as canonical.
4. Carry forward implementation obligations, open risks, and validation requirements in one place.
close_reason: Integrated the ownership guarantee boundary, invariants, concrete rules, deliberate exclusions, examples, and validation implications into the canonical language and implementation docs.

title: Define the exact Ferox safe-code guarantee boundary and core ownership invariants
description: Before the ownership model can be finalized, Ferox needs a precise statement of what safe code guarantees and invariants it commits to. This task defines the guarantee boundary for memory safety and data-race safety, the core semantic invariants that must always hold, and the high-level safety model that later ownership and borrowing rules must preserve.
design:
Primary question: What exact guarantees and semantic invariants must Ferox safe code preserve, independent of specific borrow-checking rules?

Define:
1. The precise boundary of Ferox's safe-code commitment for memory safety and data-race safety.
2. The core semantic invariants that must hold for ownership, aliasing, mutation, and sharing.
3. The assumptions about unsafe or privileged escape hatches, if any.
4. The classes of bugs that Ferox explicitly does and does not claim to prevent.

This task should establish the target that the ownership rule set must satisfy.
close_reason: Defined the safe-code guarantee boundary, core ownership invariants, explicit non-goals, boundary examples, and validation implications in spec/LANGUAGE.md and spec/IMPLEMENTATION.md.

title: Define the concrete Ferox ownership and borrowing rules, including deliberate exclusions
description: Once the guarantee boundary is clear, Ferox needs a concrete rule set that preserves it. This task defines the actual ownership and borrowing rules, the intentionally forbidden patterns relative to Rust, and the checker-facing shape of the model from a language-design perspective.
design:
Primary question: What ownership and borrowing rules should Ferox actually adopt to preserve the guarantee boundary while staying smaller and more restrictive than Rust?

Define:
1. Core ownership transfer, borrowing, mutation, and aliasing rules.
2. The role of lexicality, lifetime scope, and any simplified borrow restrictions.
3. Deliberately rejected Rust patterns and why forbidding them improves Ferox.
4. The shape of checker obligations from the language-rule perspective.

This task should turn invariants into a concrete rule system with accepted and rejected examples.
close_reason: Defined the concrete v1 ownership and borrowing rules, deliberate exclusions, accepted/rejected examples, and validation implications in spec/LANGUAGE.md and spec/IMPLEMENTATION.md.

title: Decide: stop attended sessions from handing off early
description:
## Why

In attended sessions, agents stop after one or two beads, or offer "continue or handoff?", when they have used 10–30% of a 1M window. The owner has had to correct this in at least seven sessions. Each early handoff costs another prime and another round of owner attention. The agent's own context estimate is also unreliable: one session said it was at "about 230k tokens", and the owner answered "we have context enough.. continue".

## Evidence

Owner corrections (session prefix, UTC date, quote):
- 3748816d, 2026-10-19: "the limit of context is 600k. we have room"
- 119d07a5, 2026-10-19: "we have tons of context, you do more stuff now", then "we only used 10%"
- 73454788, 2026-10-19: "we have a lot of context continue fx-origin-syntax-trial-u49"
- 0c465b0b, 2026-10-19: "we have context enough.. continue"
- e1f15d82, 2026-10-19: "we are at 20% ctx used, so we can maybe continue"
- f54f050d, 2026-10-20: "we only used 20% of ctx. what is next?"
- 319fa31b, 2026-10-21: "contineu", answering a stop at about 230k
- c697036a, 2026-10-21: the owner agreed with an audit finding that sessions hand off at 230–300k, though the rule allows up to 400k

Current owners and why they failed:
- AP-SESSION-001 (canonical) sets when to stop adding scope (400k) and when to hand off (600k). It sets no floor, so stopping early never breaks it. Ambiguous.
- The agent cannot see its real context use, so it guesses, and it guesses high. Missing.
- The user memory `session-length-400k` (2026-10-21) is wording only and is not loaded outside this owner's machine. No session since it was written has been attended, so it is unproven.
- `scripts/autorun.sh` (fx-3md) chains sessions only in unattended runs. It does not apply to attended sessions.

## Scope

In scope:
- the project's Claude Code hooks (`.claude/settings.json` or a hook script under `scripts/`)
- if needed, one line in `.agent-protocols.local.md` with a re-render of `AGENTS.md`

Out of scope:
- AP-SESSION-001's text. A floor belongs in the Starcompass source repository; propose it there only if the owner asks.
- `scripts/autorun.sh`

## Acceptance

- In an attended session that closes a bead below 350k context with a ready, non-epic bead that is not labelled `owner`, the agent picks the next bead without asking. Observed in one behavior trial with a fresh agent.
- The agent's stated context use is within 10% of the transcript's real `usage` count.

## Implementation Notes

Recommended enforcement, highest that works:
1. Structure: add a hook (UserPromptSubmit and Stop) that reads the transcript's last assistant `usage` (input + cache read + cache creation tokens) and prints `context: <N>k of 1000k`, so the agent stops guessing.
2. Mechanical check: add a Stop hook that blocks the stop once, with a reason, when context is under 350k, `br ready` lists a pickable bead, no bead is in progress for this session, and the last assistant message proposes a handoff or a fresh session. Allow the second stop, so the owner is never trapped.

Rejected:
- More wording in AGENTS.md: the memory already says this, and wording is what failed.
- Using `scripts/autorun.sh` for attended work: it gives up the owner's interjections, which they use.

## Verification

- A hook unit test feeds a recorded transcript tail at 250k and 450k, and checks that the hook reports the count and blocks only in the first case.
- Behavior trial: a fresh attended-style session closes a small bead and goes on to the next one.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if Claude Code hooks cannot read transcript usage. Fall back to the reporting hook only.
- Stop if the owner rejects a Stop hook that can block in attended sessions.

## Maintenance Notes

- A Stop hook can misfire on conversational answers, so it must match only handoff proposals and block at most once per stop.
- Related: fx-hbs (parallel agent fronts) changes how many sessions run at once, not how long each runs.

title: Decide: parallel agent fronts in Tide
description:
## Decision

Should Tide run several agent sessions at once as standing "fronts", each owning
one area of work, and if so, which fronts and what rules keep them from
colliding?

Owner call (scope and direction, AP-SCOPE-001): the owner said on 2026-10-21
that they will review the first parallel run and decide whether separate fronts
are worth it. Recommendation: adopt two fronts at most until the review loop is
trimmed (fx-eit), with the shared-resource rules below written into the
overlay.

## Why

On 2026-10-21 three Tide sessions ran at once: an older session holding fx-3md
(dirty in the main checkout) and fx-gcs.1 (its own worktree), plus tide-96
(fx-e3t) and tide-8b (fx-t99), each in its own worktree and branch. This was
the first parallel run. Whether it pays for itself has not been judged.

## Evidence

What the run showed:
- Claiming with `br` before starting, plus one worktree and branch per bead,
  kept the sessions apart. Two short cross-session messages split the ready
  beads.
- `design/reference.md` is a shared budget, at 24,996 of D14's 25,000 tokens.
  Two sessions that both change the core reference compete for it. The
  sessions agreed to ask each other before spending any core tokens.
- The main checkout is the merge bottleneck. fx-gcs.1 was approved through r9
  but could not fast-forward `main`, because another session had uncommitted
  README.md edits in the main tree.
- The review loop (`GOVERNANCE.md`, Merge Rule) costs more than drafting, so
  more fronts add review load in proportion. fx-eit measures that loop.

## Scope

In scope:
- Whether to run fronts, how many, and how work is split: by bead, by design
  chapter, or by kind (design, conformance corpus, tooling).
- Rules for shared resources: the core token budget, the main checkout, the
  merge order onto `main`, and `.beads/issues.jsonl` written by several
  sessions.
- Whether the session runner (fx-3md) should start fronts or stay serial.

Out of scope:
- The review loop itself (fx-eit).
- Any change to the supervisor merge rule.

## Acceptance

- The owner records the decision on this bead: no fronts, or named fronts with
  their areas.
- If fronts are adopted, `.agent-protocols.local.md` states the shared-resource
  rules above, rendered into AGENTS.md with a clean drift check.

## Notes

- Inputs: the fx-e3t, fx-t99, fx-3md, and fx-gcs.1 histories (comments,
  reviews, commits), and how long each waited on another session.
- A front-per-chapter split would clash with beads that cross chapters, such as
  fx-e3t (03 and the core reference).

title: Turn the query-oriented compiler direction into an explicit Ferox architecture commitment
description: Ferox now points toward query-oriented compiler services, incremental checking, and reusable tool-facing compiler data, but the commitment is still too architectural and fuzzy. This task is to define the intended compiler service model more concretely: what should be query-based, what stable identities and caches are needed, what outputs should be exposed to tools, and how the compiler architecture should support fast feedback, refactors, and future verification work.
design:
Primary question: What compiler architecture best delivers Ferox's safe-change tooling contract and fast feedback goals?

Define the intended architecture in terms of:
1. Core queries/services: parse, lower, resolve, type/ownership check, diagnostics, symbol graph, checked IR, formatting support.
2. Stable identities and cache boundaries: files, packages, modules, items, symbols.
3. Incrementality model: what invalidates what, and how single-file edits stay cheap.
4. Service reuse: how CLI, IDEs, refactors, and future verification tooling share the same engine.

The outcome should be an explicit architectural commitment, not just an implementation preference.
acceptance_criteria:
Done means this task answers all of the following clearly:
- Which compiler functions are explicit reusable queries/services?
- What stable IDs and cache boundaries does the system require?
- How does the architecture support fast incremental check and machine-safe rewrites?
- What architectural choices are deliberately out of scope for V1?

Include:
- a small service graph and rationale for why this architecture best fits Ferox;
- a downstream implementation validation plan with unit tests for invalidation and cache behavior, corpus tests for incremental correctness, and end-to-end scripts for repeated edit/check/refactor flows;
- detailed logging and trace requirements for query execution, invalidation, cache hits/misses, and service reuse paths.
close_reason: Defined the query-oriented compiler architecture in spec/IMPLEMENTATION.md, including service graph, identities, cache boundaries, invalidation, reuse, validation, and tracing expectations.

title: Tide-in-Eon adoption ladder: measured gates for Tide crates in Eon
description:
# Tide-in-Eon adoption ladder (draft for Lucca, revision 2, 2026-11-13)

Agreed between the Tide coordinator and eon-desk at Lucca's request ("see if you can agree in some more beads that will path till eon adoption in some parts of eon"). The baseline is eon-desk's `tide-in-eon-report.md`: no adoption now, a protocol crate first, Runtime lifecycle as the real prize.

Revision 2 takes all nine of eon-desk's changes. eon-overseer reviews the gates for Eon's build and test infrastructure. The Eon decision is Lucca's (Eon AGENT-RULES "Implementation Languages": an explicit decision naming the subsystem advantage and accepting the toolchain cost, plus a version policy and exit condition per AP-REFERENCE-001).

**Tide cannot make Eon compile faster.** It is rustc plus an admission driver, so every build gate is "no measurable regression". The payoff is defects caught:

- seeded deterministic replay of lifecycle races;
- contracts and property tests on codecs;
- authority diffs.

**Measurement rule for every build gate:**

- medians of 5 or more runs, in a booked quiet slot;
- clean and incremental builds;
- on the same machine and Eon commit as the baseline.

**Out of scope, with no path:** Venus/wgpu, libghostty FFI, Orbit's PTY host, and the authority layer of the agent CLI.

**Order:** Tide's E1 gate and first demo come first. Eon has priority over Tide.

## Stage 0: out-of-tree fixture, no Eon edits (may run anytime)

- **Tide fx-vjvb.** Eon's `eon-workspace-protocol` and `orbit/crates/protocol`, pinned at one Eon commit, admitted under tide-admit. Their own tests pass, with EONW and ORBS golden bytes unchanged. Each blocker is beaded.
- **Gates to stage 1:**
  - Tide E1 passes (fx-ic2);
  - the first demo passes (fx-nkv.7, fx-nkv.8);
  - fx-vjvb admits both crates with 25 or fewer mechanical edits.

## Stage 1: pilot, `eon-workspace-protocol` as a Tide crate in Eon

- **Timing.** No Eon edit before Eon's v0.2.0 cut.
- **Tide prerequisites:**
  - fx-7m6f, RUST-6: Eon's pinned stable toolchain consumes the crate through the Cargo.toml export. Eon's toolchain has no nightly.
  - fx-1n5n, Nix: a hermetic `nix build`, with no `/usr/bin/cc` and no `~/.rustup`.
  - The aarch64-darwin target bead. The crate is in Eon's macOS preview build (mac-launch kz4p).
  - fx-v4c9: strict, tagged codecs.
  - The build-cost benchmark bead.
  - The codec-defect bead.
- **Entry gates.** All are measured on the fixture before any Eon edit:
  - **(a) Green.** Eon's `nix build` and `eon-test` pass on x86_64-linux and aarch64-darwin, with Venus and Runtime unchanged.
  - **(b) Build time.** Both of these hold:
    - Eon's full workspace, clean and incremental, within +3%;
    - the crate's incremental rebuild within +10%.
  - **(c) Memory.** Peak RSS per compiler or driver process is within +10%, and never over the 6 GiB per-process cap (heavy.sh; eon-os2bi).
  - **(d) Wire.** EONW golden bytes and codec fixtures are unchanged, byte for byte.
  - **(e) Value.** Contracts or property tests catch at least one planted codec defect that today's `eon-test` misses.
  - **(f) Edits.** 25 or fewer admission edits, all mechanical.
  - **(g) Revert.** One commit returns the crate to plain Rust.
- **Exit condition.** Revert per (g) if Tide blocks an Eon toolchain bump to Eon's pinned stable for more than 1 week, or if any gate regresses.
- **Eon side,** filed by eon-desk after Lucca approves:
  - the implementation-language decision, with its version policy and exit condition;
  - the stage-1 pilot bead, gated on everything above.

## Stage 2: `orbit/crates/protocol`

- The same gates as stage 1, with ORBS golden bytes unchanged.
- Starts after stage 1 has held for 2 weeks with no revert.

## Stage 3: Runtime supervisor lifecycle (the `supervisor.rs` lease and reap paths)

- **Tide prerequisites:**
  - fx-ssek: Unix sockets with SO_PEERCRED;
  - fx-f6xp: the sim.world.proc design, then its implementation bead;
  - fx-m0f5: planted-fault controls;
  - fx-nkv.7: replay manifests.
- **Entry gates:**
  - **(a) Races.** Eon's real supervisor code, pinned and ported into the fixture (not only a hand-written model), reproduces at least 2 historical Eon races (eon-awmq.6 reap, eon-l4e7s deadline). Each replays deterministically by seed, and each is found within 1,000 seeds.
  - **(b) Build cost.** Stage 1's build-time and memory gates hold on the larger code.
  - **(c) Flakes.** The ported module passes `eon-test`, and the path's flake rate does not rise over 4 weeks against a baseline measured over 4 weeks before the port. eon-desk files the baseline bead.

## This epic

Tracks Tide's side of the ladder. Its blockers are the Tide prerequisites for the stage-1 and stage-3 gates. It closes when stage 1's Tide gates (a) to (g) are measured as passing on the fixture. Stage 3's Tide beads stay linked, labelled eon-adoption.

It is not a milestone (AP-MILESTONE-001 needs Lucca's approval for one). It does not change E1's or the first demo's priority, and Eon keeps priority over Tide. Eon-side beads, filed by eon-desk after Lucca approves: the implementation-language decision with its version policy and exit condition, the flake-rate baseline, and the stage-1 pilot.

Source: Lucca, 2026-11-13 ~01:05Z, to the Tide coordinator: "talk with the eon-desk / see if you can agree in some more beads that will path till eon adoption in some parts of eon". eon-desk's revision is folded in, and eon-overseer's infrastructure check is pending.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Revision 3 (2026-11-13 ~01:15Z). eon-overseer's infrastructure check judged the ladder workable after Eon's v0.2.0 cut and asked for 5 changes, which eon-desk and the Tide coordinator accepted.
(1) Memory gate (c): no per-process cap exists in heavy.sh. A wrapper (RUSTC_WRAPPER, or systemd-run --scope with memory accounting) measures peak RSS for each rustc and Tide driver process: within +10%, hard ceiling 6 GiB. The wrapper lives in fx-ayxr.
(2) Timing gate (b): run interleaved ABAB pairs across quiet slots and report medians and the coefficient of variation. If CV is over 1%, raise N rather than call a 3% difference. Budget about 2 quiet slots per side, about 20 workspace builds; mark noisy runs and rebook them.
(3) Darwin: gate (a) must be green on both platforms; gates (b) and (c) are measured on x86_64-linux only, because mac timing capacity is noisy or costs money. The darwin half needs Eon's mac-launch path (kz4p) first.
(4) Gates (d) and (g) stand. Any wire change at all needs a version bump, never an in-place amendment.
(5) Stage 3's flake baseline needs an Eon-side collector first (nextest JUnit in eon-test, kept by land-checks.sh and heavy.sh, with a named test set; eon-r2lok counted separately).
Stage 0 runs at low priority anytime but books no quiet slots before the cut. The full text is in the coordinator's ladder file, revision 3.

title: TCP through Net: bind, connect, and simulated loopback
description:
## Why

E1's gate run (fx-ic2) needs this surface to execute on the checked toolchain:
`trials/e1-checked/protocol.md` §10.1 lists it as E1-P8, and no existing bead owns it. fx-o8o's map:
C10 fails on E0432 for net::{TcpListener, TcpStream}.

## Evidence

- `trials/e1-checked/protocol.md (§10.1 row E1-P8, §10.2)`
- `design/reference.md §6.1, §6.7`

## Scope

Net::bind, Net::connect, TcpListener (accept, incoming, local_addr), TcpStream (io::Read/io::Write,
also for &TcpStream; peer_addr, shutdown), keeping Rust's API without ambient bind/connect
(FX0501), and Net attenuations only/no_bind, real and simulated, with network operations as
checkpoints whose cancellation error has io::ErrorKind::Cancelled. The io traits and io::Error are
fx-ecb's. Net::get and HTTP are outside this bead. Production std under crates/, built and admitted
through tide-admit; no new language semantics. Protocol §2 held-out rules apply.

## Acceptance

Two tasks in one simulation connect over a simulated loopback address and exchange bytes
deterministically per seed; a no_bind Net cannot bind; real loopback works in the harness sandbox;
local_addr reports the bound simulated or real address; E1 task C10 no longer fails on
net::{TcpListener, TcpStream}. Toolchain tests prove each item executes, not only type-checks.
Std API changes must also satisfy fx-nkv acceptance on production/conformance equivalence; the
production library owns runtime behavior.
close_reason: Landed: TCP through Net, real and simulated loopback. Codex r1 (5 blocking findings, fixed), r2 approve; Opus r3 (one test-only blocking finding, fixed), r4 approve. Landing suites on 051817f: workspace 267/0, conformance 299/12 AWAITS/0 FAIL, harness 69 OK, E1 references 29 pass (C10 now passes).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Held-out rule (trials/e1-checked/protocol.md §2), recorded by plan review 2026-11-09: until the E1 gate report is published, copy no E1 task, checked case, reference solution or writer program from trials/e1-checked/ into design/, the reference or companion, a diagnostic's text, an example, a conformance case or a toolchain test, and base no such change on those files. Running an E1 reference to confirm this bead's surface no longer fails is allowed. A breach is recorded on fx-ic2 and needs a fresh held-out task set.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Design decisions 2026-11-10 (coordinator Opus, from Fable research /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/tide-research-chan/report.md §§1.9-1.13 and §4 items 5-14): adopt the report's recommendations.
1. Net shape: address argument through a sealed trait so Rust's call sites compile; SocketAddr/IpAddr/Ipv4Addr/Ipv6Addr/Shutdown re-exported as plain data; resolve only IP literals and localhost in this bead (real side: other names via Rust's resolver, recorded as a limit; sim: other names fail). 03 §12.3's ':7000' is node-tier, not accepted here.
2. Attenuation: no_bind() -> bind PermissionDenied; only(hosts) -> connect to an unlisted address PermissionDenied, literal case-insensitive host match, IPs compared parsed, exact port, never via lookup; only doesn't limit bind or accepted peers.
3. Surface: Rust's bind/accept/incoming/local_addr, connect, Read/Write for TcpStream and &TcpStream, peer_addr/local_addr/shutdown; flush no-op; checkpoints bind/connect/accept/read/write/shutdown; local_addr/peer_addr none. incoming() in a cancelled scope yields the error once then None (stdin.lines() precedent). read_owned/write_owned/try_clone/options/timeouts out of scope.
4. Real backend: Rust sockets set non-blocking; each op loops cancel check -> call -> on WouldBlock poll(2) on the socket plus a per-thread wake eventfd, bounded by the earliest enclosing deadline (fx-o8j/fx-zc1's wait primitive).
5. Sim loopback: SimNet in sim state, one mutex never across a point, BTreeMaps, simulation-local ids; host 127.0.0.1 (0.0.0.0 listens there); port 0 drawn from 49152..=65535 on the net sub-stream; AddrInUse; dropped listener frees its port; backlog 128 (connect returns before accept); 65,536 bytes per direction; lazy delivery via segments with arrive = max(now+latency, previous). Latency uniform 1-10 ms per packet on the net sub-stream; per-op model in the report's §1.12 (connect = one round trip, atomic at wake; refused -> ConnectionRefused); network waits cancellable.
6. Equivalence: one suite run on real 127.0.0.1:0 and sim.net comparing values/ErrorKinds, excluding ports and timing; timing-dependent cases assert the allowed set. Linux only.
Out of scope, reported only: 03 §2.6's seccomp list refuses sockets; whether RUN-3 later admits loopback for tests is RUN-3's owner's question (fx-hxw's Acceptance can pass now under rustc's ordinary harness).

title: Decide channel, filesystem, network, and simulator-setup details left open by the E1 dialect round
description:
## Why

## Evidence

trials/e1-dialect/grading.md §5 (each gap names its reference section and normative source):
- G3: channel errors. Rust's unit `RecvError` and reason-less `SendError(T)` cannot say that a
  checkpoint failed because of cancellation; reference 7.2 implies `is_cancelled()` on channel
  errors, 03 §1.1 promises it only for capability errors. Also state that a disconnect is not an
  echo (03 TASK-2 already implies it).
- G4: whether a crash before `sync_dir` leaves a renamed target old-or-new or can lose the entry
  (03 §9.5, D15); then the atomic-replace pattern in reference 6.3.
- G5: `NetError::is_transient`'s cases and the simulated cost of one `Net::get` (03 §9.3).
- G6: `Fs::read_dir`'s item type, which `DirEntry` methods ADMIT-1 admits, and whether
  `OsStr`/`OsString` keep their Rust API (03 §1.1, ADMIT-1).
- G9: whether `Stdin` reads are inherent; parameter types of `world.args` and `world.stdin`;
  whether a `world.http` peer closure must be `Send` (03 §1.1, §9.2).

## Scope

In scope: decide each of G3, G4, G5, G6, G9 in its owning chapter (03, with 01 D7/D15 where a
decision changes), then update the reference (6.1, 6.3, 6.7, 6.8, 7.1-7.3) or companion 17.

Out of scope: contract semantics (the sibling bead for G10-G12); implementing std.

## Acceptance

- 03 decides each item, with the reasoning, and drops the matching "provisional" markers.
- The reference or companion states each decision; the core stays under D14's budget
  (24,989 of 25,000 tokens; recount with scripts/count-tokens.sh; detail goes to the companion).
- A review round in reviews/ finds no contradiction among 01, 03, and the reference pair.

## Implementation Notes

1. Prefer Rust's API wherever it can carry the meaning (D18: a Tide program is valid Rust); a
   departure needs a stated reason, as `Shared::new(v, tasks)` has.
2. For G4, POSIX rename atomicity is the reading every atomic-replace protocol needs; check what
   the simulator's crash model (03 §9.5) must then guarantee.
3. Docs-only design work: review rounds, not converge (GOVERNANCE.md).

## Verification

- `grep -n provisional design/reference.md` no longer marks the decided items.
- The review file's verdict is approve or approve with notes.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop and ask the owner if a decision changes a D-level rule in 01 (D7, D15, D18).
close_reason: Decided G3, G4, G5, G6, G9 in 03 and D15; reference pair updated (core 24,995 tokens); rounds 25-28, round 28 approves with notes.

title: Execute and grade paired E1 on the checked toolchain
description:
## Why

D0 requires a paired learnability experiment on the checked toolchain; prior stub metadata builds do
not establish its executable gate.

## Evidence

- `design/01-design.md (D0, D11, D14, D15, D18)`
- `design/03-authority-concurrency.md (ROOT, TASK, LOCK, authority and replay rules)`
- `conformance/README.md (stub oracle limitations)`
- `trials/e1-checked/protocol.md` (frozen by fx-gfq), `trials/e1-checked/readiness.md` (fx-o8o's
  first-failure map and remaining work)

## Scope

Run E1 as trials/e1-checked/protocol.md fixes it. fx-gfq (protocol) and fx-o8o (harness, suites,
reference solutions) are closed; every protocol §10.1 prerequisite and the gate machinery (fx-rpwp)
block this bead. Keep status OPEN with dependency edges, not a sticky manual BLOCKED status. Before
the first writer session, record on this bead each §10.2 readiness item with its evidence: every
prerequisite closed; every reference solution passes ./check, its structure check and its
acceptance suite in both arms, Tide through the driver and production std, with no R or L
placeholder left in harness.py; E1-P14's FX conformance; the suites, structure checks and render
script frozen with their tree SHA-256; the sandbox, canaries and identities from fx-rpwp; the trial
order. Gate operations (comments of 2026-11-08): no concurrent heavy I/O, cargo-sweep.timer not due,
a tmpfs TMPDIR for the Rust arm's fixtures or proof the fsync exposure is gone on the gate machine;
graders review every integrity-flagged record before scoring. Every used check/test/API must
execute under the checked toolchain; metadata-only stubs cannot satisfy it. Running this experiment
completes on a truthful reproducible report including failure, while the language validation gate
remains failed/open if thresholds fail. Fresh isolated writers in bounded batches keep the
coordinator below about 100k context, with raw logs outside its context. Not blocked on fx-nkv
merely by preference; no asserted ordering of E3 before E1. Preserve D0's 0.8x first-check,
final-pass >= Rust, <=1.5x iterations. Protocol §2's held-out rules bind everyone until the report is
published.

## Acceptance

Publish a reproducible measured paired report: first-check >= 0.8x Rust, final pass >= Rust,
iterations <= 1.5x Rust. Used APIs and tests must execute through the checked toolchain. Report
failure truthfully: completing this experiment does not make a failed language gate pass.
close_reason: E1 gate report published (a029f11): all three §8 thresholds met

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Recorded from fx-o8o round 2 (Opus decision, 2026-11-08): grading reads the acceptance verdict from inside the process. A Rust candidate runs in the same process as the acceptance tests, so it can in principle forge libtest output. fx-o8o mitigates this by freezing each suite's expected test list and statically flagging forging constructs (process::exit or abort, pre-main hooks, printed result lines) for grader review, with the same rule for both arms. Tide can't forge this way: exit is FX0501, and unsafe needs a grant. During the gate, graders must review every flagged record before scoring.

comments.text:
Gate operations constraint, recorded from fx-o8o's proof (2026-11-08):
- The protocol gives each test a 10-second wall limit. B9's Rust reference fsyncs the store file and its directory, and once, under heavy shared disk I/O, it exceeded that limit, although it normally passes (5/5 alone).
- The owner's weekly cargo-sweep timer (Sun 03:00) deletes build fingerprints under the checkout's target/ while a build is running.
So run the gate with no concurrent heavy I/O and with cargo-sweep.timer not due. Otherwise a correct writer solution, especially one that fsyncs, can fail for reasons outside its code.

E1 GATE RUN PROCEDURE (fx-ic2.2), for every gate slot fx-ic2.3 to fx-ic2.6. The batch beads quote
it.

**Fixed names.**
- R = 675c26e126df6db6090a94ddde6acc8004fe454d (main after the fx-ic2.8 CLI 2.1.321 fix; the earlier R 147eb9a and its run dir are archived as run-147eb9a, never started).
- G = /home/lucca/pjs/lab/tide/.worktrees/fx-ic2: detached at R; nobody commits in it or moves it.
- RUN = /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/tide-e1-gate/run (J = 2, initialized 2026-11-14T19:24:15Z; order hash 9d0951c1…5c50, unchanged).
- T = /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/tide-e1-gate/ic2.2: holds preflight.sh, summary.py and
  probe-under-load.sh.
- HEAVY = ~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/heavy.sh.

Every command runs from G.

**0. Once per boot, before the first slot.**
The canary and probe records carry a key: the harness file hashes, the bwrap version and the boot
ID. `run` refuses unless both canaries and the probe match the current key.
- Canaries into RUN, one heavy run each:
  `bash HEAVY env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4 timeout 900 python3 trials/e1-checked/harness.py canary rust RUN/rust-canary.json </dev/null`,
  then the same command with `tide` and `RUN/tide-canary.json`. Each must exit 0.
  Done for this boot at 19:26Z: both passed with the current key.
- Probe: `T/probe-under-load.sh`, which needs the credential in its environment. It must report
  `passed: true`, with the 3 outside requests denied, both inside controls without error, and
  end_reason `done`. Passed for this boot at 19:24Z under two dry writers (load 5.6-6.7).
- After a reboot: rerun both canaries. Move `probe.json`, `probe-session/`, `probe-writer/` and
  any `probe-outside` aside to `RUN/probe-boot-<old boot id>/` and rerun the probe, which refuses
  existing paths.
- A reboot in the middle of a batch leaves an unfinished attempt. The next `run` resumes it as a
  host interruption, which reruns it once.

**1. Booking.** Each slot is booked with eon-overseer as E1-exclusive, with length L from the
formula below. While it runs, Tide runs no other agent: the two writers fill Tide's two-agent cap.

**2. Preflight, at slot start.**
`QUIET_LOG=<file> bash T/preflight.sh RUN L --scan </dev/null`. Exit 0 and a final
`PREFLIGHT PASS` are required. On any FAIL, start nothing and comment on the batch bead.

It checks:
- the 1-minute load is below 12;
- heavy.sh's `quiet-until` has passed;
- now..now+L stays out of the standing quiet slots. Nothing starts that could run past 02:55Z or
  14:55Z. After a standing slot, a QUIET OVER line must exist: a line matching
  `^<ts> eon-overseer: QUIET OVER` in QUIET_LOG, with ts after that day's 02:55Z or 14:55Z;
- no booking in eon-overseer/quiet-slots.txt (`book-quiet.sh --list`) overlaps now..now+L;
- cargo-sweep.timer and nix-profile-trim.timer (user) and apt-daily-upgrade.timer (system) are not
  due before now+L;
- G is at R and clean;
- RUN's rust and tide canaries and its probe say `passed` with the current key;
- then the pre-run store scan, `coordinator.py store-scan RUN`, run directly since it compiles
  nothing. It writes `RUN/store-before.json`. When its only output is
  `E1 coordinator stopped: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '/nix/store/<…>.drv.chroot…'`, a Nix
  build ended during the scan, and the scan reruns once. Any other failure, or a second failure, is
  fatal: do not start.

QUIET_LOG: no file under eon-overseer/ receives the QUIET OVER lines. They are written by hand into
each agent's `~/.cache/eon-agents/<agent>-work/INBOX.md`. Set QUIET_LOG to the inbox eon-overseer
writes Tide's QUIET OVER to. Without QUIET_LOG, preflight checks only `quiet-until`, which heavy.sh
itself honors and eon-overseer extends when a slot runs long, and prints a NOTE.

**3. Slot length.**
L = P + (⌈N/J⌉ + F) · (W + G), in minutes.
- N = trials in the batch; J = 2.
- P = 10: preflight with store scan, plus canaries when needed.
- W = 41: the 40-min session limit (SESSION_SECONDS 2400) plus prepare and freeze.
- G = 10 per trial for grading. The dry runs at R measured 15 s, 24 s and up to 36 s (readiness).
  The margin covers a first grade (compile only) and a final grade at its 480 s aggregate deadline.
- F = 1: a reserve for one fault rerun. A rerun starts at once in the same worker and cannot be
  stopped without cancelling the run. With J = 2 a rerun of an early slot overlaps later slots,
  but a fault on the last slot to start adds one full wave.

The worst case beyond that (two faults, or grading retries at the 600 s guard) is not reserved; the
run timeout covers it.
Latest start = (next 02:55Z or 14:55Z cutoff, or next booking) − L.

**4. Run command.**
```
cd /home/lucca/pjs/lab/tide/.worktrees/fx-ic2
bash ~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/heavy.sh env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4 timeout $(( (L - 10) * 60 )) \
  bash -c '[ "$(date +%s)" -le LATEST_START_EPOCH ] || { echo "late grant $(date -u +%TZ)"; exit 75; };
           echo "grant $(date -u +%FT%TZ) load $(cut -d" " -f1 /proc/loadavg)";
           exec python3 trials/e1-checked/coordinator.py run /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/tide-e1-gate/run --batch N' \
  </dev/null >>/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/tide-e1-gate/batch-<bead>.log 2>&1
```
`run` takes the first N pending positions in the frozen order. It goes through heavy.sh, for these
reasons:
1. The run compiles Rust and runs compiled writer code in its jails, which AGENTS.md's Heavy-runs
   rule puts behind heavy.sh.
2. Holding heavy.sh's slot keeps every other heavy run off the machine for the whole batch. That is
   what makes the slot E1-exclusive, which the 2026-11-14 03:30Z CPUWeight=1 decision requires so
   that a starved test does not time out as a candidate failure.
3. heavy.sh holds the start during a quiet window.

Side effects:
- heavy.sh's `nice -n 19` reaches the coordinator, the writer CLIs and the jails, since
  `systemd-run --scope` inherits it. It applies equally to every trial and both arms.
- heavy.sh's CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=6 is ignored: the harness pins 4 itself.
- The LATEST_START check stops a late heavy.sh grant from running into a quiet slot (exit 75: no
  writer started).
- The `timeout` is only a backstop at the booked end. If it fires, SIGTERM cancels the run (exit
  130). The trial in flight becomes a host interruption and is rerun on the next `run`.

Never interrupt a batch on purpose. Exit codes: 0 means the batch is done. 2 prints
`E1 coordinator stopped: <reason>` on stderr and means operator action: confinement breach,
identity change, grading exhausted after two retries, or a store-scan failure. Then start no
further batch until the reason is recorded on fx-ic2.

**5. After the slot.**
- `python3 -I T/summary.py RUN FIRST LAST` prints only counts, statuses, times and tokens. Paste
  its output into the batch comment. Nobody reads writer logs, prompts or sources in the
  coordinating context.
- `git -C G rev-parse HEAD` is R, and `git -C G status --porcelain` is empty.
- `tail -3` of the batch log shows the grant line and the exit.

**6. Batch comment fields**, on the batch bead with a copy on fx-ic2:
- bead; positions FIRST-LAST and their triples; R; RUN;
- booking: start and L;
- preflight: result, store-scan tries and exit, load;
- times: heavy.sh grant time, run exit code and time, load at start and end;
- per position, from summary.py:
  - triple and complete flag;
  - reruns, attempt, end_reason and fault name;
  - runs used, writer minutes, grading seconds and grading tries;
  - first-grade and final-grade exit (mechanical, before the concurrency and integrity review);
  - integrity flag count;
  - audit passed, error count, breach count, denied-outside count;
  - turns, API retries, peak context;
  - tokens: input, output, cache read, cache write;
- batch totals: mechanical first and final passes per arm, faults, reruns, writer minutes, grading
  minutes, tokens;
- incidents: confinement breach, operator stop, late grant, quiet or timer conflict, or "none";
- next pending position; for fx-ic2.3, the cost checkpoint after trial 3;
- the statement "no raw logs, prompts or sources read in the coordinating context".

---

**Tests of the tools.**
- `summary.py`:
  - on `readiness/dry`: 4 slots, exit 0;
  - on `ic2.2/dry-tmp` and `ic2.2/dry-tmp2`: 1 complete and 3 pending, exit 0. Grading 15 s and
    24 s, writer 1.5 and 1.1 min;
  - on `run 0 3`: 4 pending, exit 0;
  - on a missing dir: exit 2.
- `preflight.sh RUN 160` at 17:01Z:
  - PASS: load, quiet-until (16:57:30Z), the three timers, G at R;
  - FAIL: both canaries and the probe missing in RUN, which is correct today.
- `preflight.sh RUN 700` with a QUIET_LOG: FAIL for the 03:00Z slot overlap, the eon-nix-times
  03:00Z booking, and a missing QUIET OVER line, as intended. `--scan` itself was not run against
  RUN: I may run only the probe there. The ENOENT match was checked against the exact readiness
  error text.
- `probe-under-load.sh`: syntax checked; refuses without a credential (exit 2). The probe part
  itself is untested.

title: E1 readiness record and gate init: protocol §10.2 items at a pinned revision
description:
## Why

trials/e1-checked/protocol.md §10.2 requires a readiness record on fx-ic2 before the first gate
writer starts. A gate run that starts with any item missing cannot report E1 as passed or failed.
`coordinator.py init` permanently fixes the trial order, its hash, the configs, `jobs`, the model,
the CLI and the identity record. So this bead also runs `init`, after the harness hardening has
landed and before fx-ic2.2's live probe, which refuses to run without an initialized state (split
review tide-fx-ic2-split/review-opus.md, findings 1, 7 and 8). Parent: fx-ic2.

## Scope

1. **Pinned revision.** Take R = main once the harness-hardening bead has landed and fx-u65 has
   closed. Create the gate worktree `.worktrees/fx-ic2`, detached at R. Nobody commits in it or
   moves it until the report bead has landed. The gate's own check compares HEAD, so any change to
   it stops the run.
2. **Before `init`: effort and parallelism.** These freeze at `init`, and the owner's later go
   (fx-ic2.3) cannot change them.
   - Choose `--jobs` J against the two-agent cap and Eon's priority, with eon-overseer's agreement.
     Record on fx-ic2 whether writer sessions count toward the two-agent cap.
   - Send the owner, through the coordinator, the pre-run estimate: about 165M input tokens, mostly
     cache reads, and 3M output, give or take 2x. Add the plan (`claude-opus-5-5` at the harness's
     default effort, protocol §3; J writers at once) and the fact that both freeze at `init`. This
     is a spending choice, so an "auto-decide" relay does not cover it.
   - `init` waits for the owner's recorded reply. If there is no reply, follow AGENTS.md's
     Autonomous runs rule: comment, set `--status blocked --add-label owner`, and end the run.
   - If the owner names a non-default effort, stop before `init`. coordinator.py passes no effort
     flag, so the harness-hardening bead reopens to add one, and this bead restarts at step 1 on
     the new main.
3. **`init`.** From the gate worktree, run `coordinator.py init <run-dir> --jobs J`, where
   `<run-dir>` is `/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/tide-e1-gate/run`, outside the repository as the
   coordinator requires. Before the first gate writer starts, a harness fix may still be needed, for
   example after a failed probe in fx-ic2.2. If so, it lands reviewed and this bead is redone at the
   new revision with a fresh run directory.
4. **Readiness evidence at R.** Every build or run goes through heavy.sh in AGENTS.md's form, with
   the load below 12. Ask the coordinator before any run longer than about 15 minutes. Record each
   §10.2 item:
   1. Every §10.1 bead is closed, plus fx-dsa, fx-ecb, fx-rpwp and the harness-hardening bead,
      shown from fx-ic2's dependency list.
   2. Every reference solution passes `./check`, its structure check and its acceptance suite in
      both arms at R. The Tide solutions do so through the driver with the production std, and
      harness.py has no R or L placeholder left.
   3. E1-P14's FX conformance for every FX code the reference names. For FX0920, FX0921 and FX0516
      the record says "excluded by owner decision 2026-11-09".
   4. The suites, structure checks and render script are frozen, with their tree SHA-256 (§6).
      Record tasks.md's SHA-256 at R, and show from `git log` that every tasks.md change since
      fx-gfq's freeze has a reason recorded on fx-ic2 (§2). Hashing and the log are enough; nobody
      needs to read the file.
   5. The §10.3 sandbox for both arms at R: harness_test, both canaries and the four-slot dry run
      pass. They can be reused from the hardening bead's landing proof only if
      `git diff <that revision> R` is empty over trials/e1-checked/, crates/,
      design/reference.md, design/reference-companion.md and the toolchain pins.
   6. Identities from state.json: the §5 toolchain identities, the exact model, the CLI path and
      version, the effort, the pinned build jobs and memory caps, J, the session limit and the
      writer argv template. Also the trial order: all 120 `(task, arm, replicate)` triples from
      state.json's `order`, which coordinator.py's `order()` builds as protocol §3 says (sorted,
      then `random.Random(20261031).shuffle`), and the full `order_hash`.

Protocol §2's held-out rules bind: nothing from trials/e1-checked/ flows into the reference, the
companion, diagnostics or examples.

## Acceptance

- fx-ic2 carries one readiness comment that names R, the run directory and §10.2 items 1-6, each
  with passing evidence at R. The comment includes the frozen tree SHA-256, tasks.md's SHA-256 with
  its change log since fx-gfq, the 120 triples and the full order hash, and the identity fields
  above.
- fx-ic2 records J with eon-overseer's agreement and the owner's reply on effort and parallelism,
  both before `init`'s timestamp in state.json.
- An item that fails stays failing on the record, and this bead stays open.

title: E1 failure classification (protocol §7.4)
description:
## Why

Protocol §7.4 requires every first-check failure and every final failure to be classified, with
evidence. A toolchain defect is flagged but never excluded. The report publishes the classification.
This bead splits the old single grading bead (split review tide-fx-ic2-split/review-opus.md,
finding 6). Parent: fx-ic2.

## Scope

Classify every first-check failure and every final failure, up to about 120. Take the failures from
the slot records, fx-ic2.7's grader-review file and its suite-test removals. Use the classes in
trials/e1-dialect/grading.md (Rust habit leaked, reference gap, design gap or contradiction,
ordinary bug), plus **toolchain defect**: a reference-taught item that does not execute, or a
toolchain bug.

- Each class gets its evidence: the diagnostic, the failing test, or the cited lines of the snapshot
  and, where relevant, of the reference.
- A toolchain defect still counts as a failure in §7.1-§7.3. It is flagged, never excluded.
- Give each trial, or each task's trials, to a fresh read-only subagent. Raw output stays on disk,
  out of the coordinator's context; subagents count toward the agent cap.
- A suspected suite dispute goes back to fx-ic2.7, which reopens.
- Protocol §2's held-out rules bind until the report is published. A reference gap or toolchain
  defect found here is recorded for the report, not fixed in the reference, the companion or
  diagnostics. An agent that has read writer programs makes no change to those documents before
  publication.

## Acceptance

- A classification file in the run directory has one entry for every first-check failure and every
  final failure in both arms. Each entry gives its class and its evidence, with toolchain defects
  flagged.
- fx-ic2 carries a comment with the file's SHA-256 and the counts per class and arm, for first check
  and final separately.

  timeout or a crash) still counts as one of the three tries. Reason: the rule affects liveness only,
  never scoring, and the harness code stays as reviewed. The run procedure never stops a run in the
  middle of a trial on purpose, so the case should not arise. This answers fx-rpwp r5's question.

  the formula with N = 3, using the dry run's grading time plus a margin, since no trial has run
  yet.

harness-hardening bead, and fx-ic2.1 is redone at the new revision with a fresh run directory. This
bead changes no protocol text, tasks or thresholds.

title: E1 gate trials 1-3 and cost checkpoint (owner's go)
description:
## Why

E1's 120 writer sessions run on `claude-opus-5-5` (protocol §3), so the full run could use most of
a week's Claude quota. An estimate from 2026-11-13 puts it at about 165M input tokens, mostly cache
reads, and 3M output, give or take 2x. The owner decides the spend from measured numbers. This bead
runs the first three trials of the frozen order and puts their measured cost to the owner.

These are counted gate trials. They are not protocol §9's metadata-only pilot, and nothing labels
them "pilot" (split review tide-fx-ic2-split/review-opus.md, findings 3-5). Parent: fx-ic2.

## Scope

**Owner go for trials 1-3 (recorded 2026-11-13).** The owner first said "we just have to stop before the spending starts", then, asked whether trials 1-3 were worth running, answered "but the Pilot ccould be worth it, nah?" and "add it". So the go covers exactly the three writer sessions at trial-order positions 1-3, plus their protocol §3 fault reruns. No session past position 3 starts without the owner's further go, recorded under this bead's cost checkpoint.

**Trials.** Run positions 1-3 of state.json's order with
`coordinator.py run /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/tide-e1-gate/run --batch 3`, from the gate
worktree `.worktrees/fx-ic2` (pinned at R by fx-ic2.1). Each session is fresh and isolated, with
protocol §4.2's budget of 20 runs and 40 minutes. Raw logs stay on disk, outside the coordinator's
context.

**Each slot follows fx-ic2.2's run procedure:**

- **Book** an E1-exclusive slot with eon-overseer.
- **Preflight**, with its output recorded in the batch comment:
  - the 1-minute load is below 12;
  - no other heavy run or concurrent heavy I/O is going;
  - cargo-sweep.timer is not due before the slot ends;
  - TMPDIR is on a tmpfs in the jail;
  - `.worktrees/fx-ic2` is clean and its HEAD is R;
  - `coordinator.py store-scan` passes.
- **Run** the whole command once through heavy.sh:
  `bash ~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/heavy.sh env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=<pinned value from the identity record> timeout <secs> python3 trials/e1-checked/coordinator.py run <run-dir> --batch N </dev/null`.
  Writer builds run inside the jail, not through heavy.sh.
- **Size N and the timeout.** Take N so that ceil(N / J) × (40 min + grading time G), plus one more
  (40 min + G) for a possible fault rerun, ends before the slot does. Set the timeout above that
  estimate and no later than the slot's end. Here N = 3. G comes from the dry run plus a margin,
  since no gate trial has run yet.
- **Never stop a run mid-trial on purpose.** A timeout or Ctrl-C is an operator cancellation. It is
  not on fx-rpwp's closed fault list, and it uses up grading tries (N3). If heavy.sh still holds the
  run when the slot starts, cancel it while it is queued, before any trial starts, and rebook.

**Faults and audit** (fx-ic2, 2026-11-12 13:31 comment; protocol §3):

- Only fx-rpwp's closed list (decisions 3 and 9) is an infrastructure fault. Budget refusal, a
  deadline kill, an early stop, and wrong or empty code are not. API throttling uses wall time
  unless the CLI ends with an error.
- An infrastructure fault gets one fresh rerun, counted. A second fault in the same slot counts the
  trial as failed.
- A tool outside the allowed set is an infrastructure fault with that single rerun.
- A denied outside-path request is counted information per arm.
- An undenied outside access is a confinement breach, and coordinator.py then refuses to continue.
  Stop, record the breach on fx-ic2, set this bead `--status blocked --add-label owner`, and end
  the run: a breach can invalidate the gate.
- Never change the gate worktree. A harness defect found once trials have run is recorded on fx-ic2,
  and this bead is set blocked. Add the owner label if the fix would change a recorded identity or
  void trials already run.

**Measure** each trial:

- input, cache-read, cache-creation and output tokens;
- the Claude quota percent drawn, from usage readings before and after;
- wall time;
- runs used;
- grading time G.

From these, project the full run's quota and calendar with a range.

**Ask the owner for the go.** Post the numbers and a recommended schedule to the owner: which quota
weeks to use and how positions 4-120 split into batch beads and slots.

- The message says that the go can set only the calendar and the batch split. The model, effort,
  J, CLI and session limit were fixed at `init` in fx-ic2.1.
- It also says what a no-go means: trials 1-3 stand, and E1 can report nothing until the run
  resumes or a fresh held-out task set is used.
- The go is a spending decision and the owner's alone; an "auto-decide" relay does not cover it.
- Until the go is recorded on fx-ic2, no fourth session starts. On a no-go or no reply, follow
  AGENTS.md's Autonomous runs rule: comment, set `--status blocked --add-label owner`, and end the
  run. This bead never closes on a no-go.

## Acceptance

- Each of trials 1-3 has a complete slot record, a first snapshot (or a record that it made no
  run), a final snapshot, its run log and its grading inputs in the run directory.
- fx-ic2 carries a batch comment with:
  - each slot's preflight output;
  - each fault with its class;
  - each rerun and each second-fault failure;
  - each tool outside the set;
  - the denied outside-path requests per arm;
  - any operator cancellation;
  - the per-trial measurements above.
- fx-ic2 carries the projection with its range, and the owner's recorded go with its batch
  schedule.

title: E1 batch 2: gate trials 41-80
description:
## Why

E1's remaining writer sessions run in bounded batches, on the schedule the owner approved after
gate trials 1-3 (fx-ic2.3). Protocol §3 keeps the coordinating session's context bounded, with raw
logs on disk (split review tide-fx-ic2-split/review-opus.md, findings 3-5). Parent: fx-ic2.

## Scope

**Trials.** Run positions 41-80 of state.json's order from the gate worktree `.worktrees/fx-ic2`
(pinned at R by fx-ic2.1), with
`coordinator.py run /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/tide-e1-gate/run --batch N`. Each session is
fresh and isolated, with protocol §4.2's budget of 20 runs and 40 minutes. Raw logs stay on disk,
outside the coordinator's context.

**Start condition.** Run only within the quota weeks named by the owner's recorded go (fx-ic2.3).
A scheduled slot that would fall outside them waits.

**Range.** `run --batch N` takes the first N incomplete slots. So before the first slot, check that
every position before 41 has a complete slot record. This bead may span several slot runs. The
coordinator may re-split the ranges of this bead and the later batch beads, using the times measured
in trials 1-3 and the owner's schedule. If it does, it updates the range in each affected bead
before that bead starts.

**Each slot follows fx-ic2.2's run procedure:**

- **Book** an E1-exclusive slot with eon-overseer.
- **Preflight**, rerun before every slot and recorded in the batch comment, since the Sunday
  cargo-sweep timer and Eon's load recur across the weeks the run spans:
  - the 1-minute load is below 12;
  - no other heavy run or concurrent heavy I/O is going;
  - cargo-sweep.timer is not due before the slot ends;
  - TMPDIR is on a tmpfs in the jail;
  - `.worktrees/fx-ic2` is clean and its HEAD is R;
  - `coordinator.py store-scan` passes.
- **Run** the whole command once through heavy.sh:
  `bash ~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/heavy.sh env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=<pinned value from the identity record> timeout <secs> python3 trials/e1-checked/coordinator.py run <run-dir> --batch N </dev/null`.
  Writer builds run inside the jail, not through heavy.sh.
- **Size N and the timeout.** Take N so that ceil(N / J) × (40 min + measured grading time G), plus
  one more (40 min + G) for a possible fault rerun, ends before the slot does. Set the timeout above
  that estimate and no later than the slot's end.
- **Never stop a run mid-trial on purpose.** A timeout or Ctrl-C is an operator cancellation. It is
  not on fx-rpwp's closed fault list, and it uses up grading tries (N3). If heavy.sh still holds the
  run when the slot starts, cancel it while it is queued, before any trial starts, and rebook.

**Faults and audit** (fx-ic2, 2026-11-12 13:31 comment; protocol §3):

- Only fx-rpwp's closed list (decisions 3 and 9) is an infrastructure fault. Budget refusal, a
  deadline kill, an early stop, and wrong or empty code are not. API throttling uses wall time
  unless the CLI ends with an error.
- An infrastructure fault gets one fresh rerun, counted. A second fault in the same slot counts the
  trial as failed.
- A tool outside the allowed set is an infrastructure fault with that single rerun.
- A denied outside-path request is counted information per arm.
- An undenied outside access is a confinement breach, and coordinator.py then refuses to continue.
  Stop, record the breach on fx-ic2, set this bead `--status blocked --add-label owner`, and end the
  run: a breach can invalidate the gate.
- Never change the gate worktree. A harness defect found mid-run is recorded on fx-ic2, and this
  bead is set blocked. Add the owner label if the fix would change a recorded identity or void
  trials already run.

## Acceptance

- Every trial in positions 41-80 has a complete slot record, a first snapshot (or a record that it
  made no run), a final snapshot, its run log and its grading inputs in the run directory.
- fx-ic2 carries a batch comment with:
  - each slot's preflight output;
  - each fault with its class;
  - each rerun and each second-fault failure;
  - each tool outside the set;
  - the denied outside-path requests per arm;
  - any operator cancellation;
  - the quota drawn and the wall time per slot.

title: E1 grader reviews: integrity flags, concurrency reviews, suite disputes
description:
## Why

Before any measure is computed, protocol §6 and fx-ic2's decision of 2026-11-08 04:03 need two
kinds of grader judgment:

- every integrity-flagged record is reviewed before scoring;
- every C1-C6 and C9 final snapshot gets a concurrency review, with its cited lines recorded per
  trial.

The measures, classification and report beads all read this bead's output. It splits the old single
grading bead, which was too big for one session (split review tide-fx-ic2-split/review-opus.md,
finding 6). Parent: fx-ic2.

## Scope

Work from the run directory `/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/tide-e1-gate/run` once all 120 slots are
complete (fx-ic2.6). Give each trial's review to a fresh read-only subagent that sees only that
trial's final snapshot, its records and the protocol rule it applies, never a reference solution.
Subagents count toward the agent cap, and their raw output stays on disk, out of the coordinator's
context.

- **Integrity flags.** For every record flagged for a forging construct (process::exit or abort, a
  pre-main hook, printed result lines), decide whether the recorded acceptance verdict stands, with
  evidence. The same rule applies to both arms. A verdict that does not stand counts as an
  acceptance failure.
- **Concurrency review** (§6), for each C1-C6 and C9 trial in both arms, about 28 in all. Fail a
  trial whose work the task says runs concurrently or in parallel does not, citing the lines. In
  particular, fail:
  - a C3 trial without one producer per input running concurrently with the merge;
  - a C5 trial whose jobs do not all start at once;
  - a C6 trial whose searches do not check for the stop at least every 4096 bytes.
- **Suite disputes** (§6). A suite may lose a test only when a disputed result shows that the test
  checks something the task text leaves open. The test is then removed from both arms' suites, and
  the decision is recorded for the report. No test is added or tightened.
  - Any regrading this causes runs from the gate worktree under the gate conditions: an
    E1-exclusive slot through heavy.sh, the run procedure's preflight, the tmpfs TMPDIR and the
    pinned build jobs. The 10-second test limit applies at grading.
  - A dispute found later, by the measures or classification bead, reopens this bead.

Protocol §2's held-out rules bind until the report is published. An agent that has read writer
programs makes no change to the reference, the companion, diagnostics or examples before then.

## Acceptance

- A grader-review file in the run directory has one entry for every flagged record and for every
  C1-C6 and C9 trial. Each entry gives the verdict, its evidence and the cited lines.
- fx-ic2 carries a comment with:
  - the file's SHA-256;
  - the counts per arm: flags reviewed, verdicts that did not stand, concurrency passes and fails;
  - every suite-test removal with its disputed result, or "none".

title: E1 harness hardening: store-closure bind, jail memory caps, pinned build jobs
description:
## Why

fx-rpwp's Opus r4 (finding 5; recorded on fx-ic2, 2026-11-12 12:30 UTC) found three gaps in the
landed E1 gate machinery under trials/e1-checked/:

- the writer jail binds all of /nix/store, because the toolchain loader lives there. The
  size-then-SHA store scan only catches byte-identical copies, so an older-revision copy of trial
  files (for example a flake `-source` at an earlier commit) is readable from inside the jail;
- the jails have no memory bound, and /tmp is a default-size RAM tmpfs on a machine shared with Eon;
- writer runs set `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4` (coordinator.py `run_writer`), but grading inherits the
  caller's environment, and heavy.sh sets 6.

These change what protocol §10.2 item 5 (sandbox) and item 6 (identities) record. `coordinator.py
init` fixes the configs, jobs, model, CLI and identity for the whole run, so this change has to land,
reviewed, before fx-ic2.1 records those items and runs `init` (split review
tide-fx-ic2-split/review-opus.md, findings 1 and 2). Parent: fx-ic2.

Its only real prerequisite is fx-rpwp, which is closed. br shows it as blocked only through the
epic's open blockers.

## Scope

Change the harness (coordinator.py, gate_checks.py, harness.py and their tests, as needed) in
`.worktrees/<this id>`:

- **Store closure bind.** The jail binds only the Nix-store closure that the recorded toolchains and
  their loader need, not all of /nix/store. The store scan also flags any store path that holds
  trials/e1-checked content, whether or not it is byte-identical to the tree.
- **Memory caps.** Each jail gets a bounded tmpfs (`bwrap --size`) and a memory cap on its process
  tree (a cgroup, for example through `systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=`, or a ulimit). The
  same caps apply to both arms and both stages (writer `./check`/`./test` and grading). Set them
  above the measured peak of every reference solution's build and suite: measure that by running the
  solutions, without reading them. Record the caps in the identity record.
- **Build jobs.** The harness itself sets one pinned `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS` for writer runs and grading,
  so nothing is inherited from the caller. It is 4 unless eon-overseer asks for less, and
  `g.identity`'s record carries it.
- **TMPDIR.** If the jail's TMPDIR does not already resolve to a tmpfs in both stages, make it do
  so, the same for both arms. The fsync and shared-I/O exposure from fx-o8o's proof hits only the
  Rust arm (fx-ic2 comments of 2026-11-08 06:17 and 06:24).
- **Effort.** Add an effort flag only if fx-ic2 records the owner's choice of a non-default writer
  effort before this candidate freezes. The flag passes the effort to the writer CLI and records it
  in launch.json and the identity. Otherwise effort stays the harness default: no flag, and
  launch.json says "default (flag not passed)".

**Added 2026-11-14 (coordinator, from the implementer's first-candidate findings).** Both block fx-ic2.1's §10.2 items, and both are harness code in the same files:

- **Tide L-stage wrapper.** `tide_library_boundary` writes `extern crate tide_candidate as solution;` at the head of the generated acceptance crate. Since fx-u65.6 (55f3ecb), the driver rejects that as FX0912 (reference §12.2), so all 26 Tide library references fail at stage L. The harness's generated code admits under the current driver: an import, not `extern crate`. No suite, reference or driver change.
- **Store scan on the gate host.** The scan byte-matches held-out content only: tasks, suites, references, reference_test.rs, reference-review.md and the gate's other non-writer material. It does not byte-match files every writer receives anyway, such as the rust/ skeleton and .gitignore, which today match thousands of unrelated store files. A store file the operator cannot read is recorded and skipped, not fatal: the jail runs as the same uid, so a writer cannot read it either. The revision-independent rule from the scope above stays.

Out of scope:

- the N3 rule (a grading try lost to an operator cancellation counts as one try). The code stays as
  reviewed, and fx-ic2.2 records why;
- protocol text, tasks, suites, reference solutions and thresholds.

Protocol §2's held-out rules bind: nothing from trials/e1-checked/ flows into the reference, the
companion, diagnostics or examples. Every build, test and dry run goes through heavy.sh in
AGENTS.md's form, with the 1-minute load below 12.

## Acceptance

- On the landed tree, harness_test passes and includes cases showing that:
  - a jailed canary cannot read a store path holding trials/e1-checked content that is not
    byte-identical to the tree;
  - the store scan flags such a path;
  - a jail process that exceeds its memory cap is killed, and the run's verdict records it;
  - `g.identity`'s record carries the pinned build jobs and the caps.
- On the landed tree, both canaries and the four-slot dry run (`coordinator.py init --dry-run`,
  then `run` and `dry-clock`, in a run directory outside the repository) pass in both arms. Inside
  the jail, TMPDIR is shown to be on a tmpfs.
- `harness.py references tide` (all 30, sandboxed) shows no stage-L failure from the wrapper. Any other failing stage is listed per task with its first diagnostic code, without suite or reference content. A harness_test case pins that the generated wrapper contains no `extern crate`.
- `coordinator.py store-scan` passes on this host. A harness_test case shows that an unreadable store file is recorded and skipped, and that a held-out byte match still fails.
- The change lands under GOVERNANCE.md's Merge Rule: a Codex pass, then an Opus converge round that
  reports instead of fixing. Each finding is fixed or rebutted, and its finder re-checks the fix or
  rebuttal.

title: E1 measures, per-trial records and bootstrap intervals (reviewed script)
description:
## Why

fx-ic2's Acceptance is a measured paired report against D0's thresholds. Protocol §7 and §8 fix the
measures, the gate and the information-only intervals. They must come out of reviewed code that
anyone can rerun from the stored records. This bead splits the old single grading bead (split review
tide-fx-ic2-split/review-opus.md, finding 6). Parent: fx-ic2.

## Scope

Write one script under trials/e1-checked/ in `.worktrees/<this id>`. Its inputs are the run
directory's slot and session records and fx-ic2.7's grader-review file. It writes a measures file
and the per-trial records. It computes:

- **Per-trial §7.4 records:**
  - every run's verdict;
  - each diagnostic code (FX, rustc E codes, lints);
  - each failing test's name;
  - the wall time and the agent turns;
  - input, cache-read, cache-creation and output tokens;
  - the peak context;
  - for Tide, the reference sections the writer read;
  - the first snapshot's size and its number of `todo!`/`hole!` holes.
- **F, P and I per arm over 60 trials** (§7.1-§7.3):
  - First-check: a trial with no run fails.
  - Final pass includes the writer's tests, the structure checks, fx-ic2.7's concurrency review and
    every acceptance test, after fx-ic2.7's integrity decisions and any suite-test removals.
  - I is the mean over trials that pass final only. If either arm has no passing trial, threshold 3
    is not met.
  - The all-60 mean, with each failure counted as 20 runs, is reported as information.
- **Each §8 threshold met or not met**, on the point estimates and in its inequality form:
  F(Tide) >= 0.8 × F(Rust), P(Tide) >= P(Rust), I(Tide) <= 1.5 × I(Rust).
- **The §8 information-only 95% intervals** for each ratio and difference. Use 10,000 bootstrap
  resamples of the 30 tasks, with both replicates and both arms of a task resampled together,
  percentile intervals, and tasks drawn with `random.Random(20261031).choices`. Report resamples in
  which a ratio is undefined, and state how wide the intervals are.
- **Counts:**
  - structure checks met only by a comment;
  - infrastructure reruns, second-fault failures, tools outside the set, denied outside-path
    requests per arm, and confinement breaches, from the slot records.

Test it with a small hand-built fixture whose answers are known first, including:

- an arm with no passing trial;
- a trial with no run;
- a zero denominator in a ratio.

Run nothing heavy. Protocol §2's held-out rules bind.

## Acceptance

- The script lands under GOVERNANCE.md's Merge Rule: a Codex pass, then an Opus converge round that
  reports instead of fixing. Each finding is fixed or rebutted and re-checked by its finder. Its
  fixture tests pass on the landed tree.
- Run at the landed revision on the stored records, it writes the measures file and the per-trial
  records.
- fx-ic2 carries a comment with:
  - the landed revision;
  - both output files' SHA-256;
  - F, P and I per arm;
  - each threshold as met or not met;
  - the intervals and their width.
close_reason: Measures script landed; all three §8 thresholds met on point estimates

title: Parallel regions: join, par_map, par_for, par_sort
description:
## Why

E1's gate run (fx-ic2) needs this surface to execute on the checked toolchain:
`trials/e1-checked/protocol.md` §10.1 lists it as E1-P5, and no existing bead owns it.

comments.text:
Design decisions 2026-11-10 (coordinator Opus, from Fable research /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/tide-research-par/report.md; the report lands in research/ as 23-parallel-regions.md with this bead): adopt the report's recommendations, with two choices made here.
1. Signatures: the conformance stub's verbatim plus par_sort: join<A,B,RA: Send,RB: Send> with Pure + Send closures; trait ParSlice<T> for [T] (prelude) with par_map (T: Pure + Sync, f: Fn + Pure + Send + Sync), par_for (T: Pure + Send), par_sort (T: Ord + Pure + Send); no par_sort_by; par_chunks_mut out of scope (03 names it, the reference and bead don't; reported).
2. Owned scoped-thread implementation, no rayon (it would supply only the scheduler; every observable rule is Tide's). Labelled partial against 03 §8.4's work-stealing pool; scheduling is unobservable, so the pool can replace it later. Threads: available_parallelism() once (par-threads key stays planned); helpers are not tasks (no Runtime registration, no CURRENT, no Tasks::limit slot, not in the deadlock report).
3. One code path over a private fork primitive: blocks claimed in index order (disjoint &mut blocks; par_map concatenates by block index); inline for len <= 1 or one worker; block size unobservable.
4. par_sort: split at len/2 to a fixed leaf size, stable-sort leaves, join halves, merge with the owned two-finger merge into an index permutation applied by swaps (report §1.4 option b; chosen over relying on driftsort so the comparison sequence depends only on the input length and survives toolchain bumps).
5. Panics: catch_unwind per branch/block, resume_unwind the lowest-index payload; an atomic stop flag stops unclaimed blocks (PAR-2); sinks buffer per block in a thread-local and append in index order up to and including the winning panic (SINK-4, PAR-1); losing branches' panic-hook output recorded as partial.
6. Simulator: sequential mode runs the work in order on the calling task's thread; no par trace events beyond the task's sink records. Mode switch: start this bead after fx-nkv.5 lands and derive the mode from CURRENT's runtime having a simulation (report option c, one owner) rather than a separate thread-local flag; if fx-nkv.5 is not landed when this bead starts, use the report's option (b) thread-local setter and fold it into the simulation identity when both have landed.
7. Nested regions and regions inside Shared::with are legal and need no extra handling (branches are Pure).

title: RUN-3 kernel sandbox for test and sim children (moved into v0)
description:
## Why
D7 decision (coordinator, owner-delegated 2026-11-15; recorded through the FX0206 bead): RUN-3, the kernel sandbox for test and simulation children, moves into the v0 tier. fx-6xi2 showed the type system alone cannot bound what admitted code reaches, because rustc has open soundness holes. Agent-written code mostly runs as tests on developer machines, so a kernel bound there covers the most frequent exposure.

- A test child that tries to reach a path or socket outside its grants is denied by the kernel, even through a capability forged via the fx-6xi2 pattern. A conformance or integration test proves this.
- The availability behaviour is documented.

title: Formally verify Tide with Bend (eventually)
description:
## Why
Owner, 2026-11-17, to tide-lead: "we have to formally verify tide with bend, eventually". fx-6xi2 and fx-iwjq showed that Tide's safety claim rests on a syntactic checker over an unsound rustc. A mechanized proof would back the claim that admitted code cannot reach authority it wasn't handed.

## Direction (tide-lead's recommendation; to scope when this starts)
- Primary target: a small core calculus of Tide's authority rules (capabilities passed from Root, admission's rejections, simulated vs real roots) and a machine-checked confinement or non-interference theorem. Secondary targets: determinism of the simulator's replay, and contract (#[requires]/#[ensures]) discharge for pure kernels (D16, fx-qzp).
- Tool: Bend's checker with --verdict, which rests on a Lean kernel (research/31 F5). Bend's checker eval reports Opus solving 20/20 tasks with checker access versus 0/20 blind. Caveats from research/31 F3: proof support is thin (few U32 lemmas, F32 axiomatic), and the source-to-kernel translation is unproved. So prove the model, not the compiler. Keep Lean 4 directly as the fallback if Bend's prover stalls.
- Tier: Later, after the alpha (fx-qlek). It doesn't block v0.

## Acceptance (for the first child, when scoped)
A checked proof artifact for the authority core calculus, a written mapping from the calculus to tide-admit's rules with each gap listed, and a CI or heavy.sh command that re-checks it.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
tide-lead, 2026-11-17: the owner flagged Harmonic's Aristotle ('these guys are interesting'). Announced 2026-11-16 (harmonic.fun/news/aristotle-rust-verification): it proves Rust has no UB and meets its spec, including inside unsafe, and proves C-to-Rust equivalence. Closed service with consumption pricing. The post names no toolchain, translation target, supported subset, spec format or proof output; Aristotle's earlier work is Lean-based, which is an inference. Case studies: Manifest (28 results, found a rounding bug) and Project 0, both Solana programs.
Candidate uses for Tide:
