title: Enforce FX0206 (CLOSURE-3) at fn-pointer coercion, conservative rule
description:
## Why
fx-6xi2 (2026-11-15; report /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/tide-6xi2/report.md) showed that tide-admit admits rustc's open #25860 pattern, including `fn keep<'a>(fs: &'a Fs) -> &'static Fs` with no `unsafe` grant. CLOSURE-3 / FX0206 is specified (design/02-memory.md §5.4, conformance/rules.md) but not enforced in crates/.

## Decision (coordinator, owner-delegated 2026-11-15)
Use a conservative rule. Reject every coercion of a fn item (local or external, std included) to a `fn` pointer when the item's signature implies outlives bounds among its lifetime parameters. It needs no region data.
Why not the precise rule: it would need implied bounds added inside MIR borrowck, and rustc's own partial fix (#129021) still misses this variant.
Cost: `closure_fnptr_accept.rs::same` becomes a reject. The diagnostic suggests a closure.
A later bead may relax this to a precise rule.

## Scope
- Implement FX0206 at the coercion site in tide-admit, and add it to `--tide-print-codes`.
- Carry fx-6xi2's two cases from branch fx-6xi2 at da8789c (conformance/cases/memory/closure_fnptr_rustc_known_bug.rs and closure_fnptr_capability.rs). Flip closure_fnptr_accept.rs::same to a reject.
- Update CLOSURE-3's text in design/02-memory.md §5.4 and conformance/rules.md.
- Record the D7 decision in design/01-design.md: RUN-3 (the Landlock and seccomp test and sim sandbox) moves into the v0 tier, tracked by its own bead. Kernel enforcement for deployed binaries stays v1. Until RUN-3 lands, public claims say safety against a malicious dependency rests on rustc's soundness, which has other open I-unsound issues.

## Acceptance
- On main, all four CLOSURE-3 cases have the expected verdict, with no AWAITS CHECKER left for FX0206.
- Full suites pass.
- GOVERNANCE.md Merge Rule: a Codex pass, then an Opus converge round. Design text changes ride the same review.

title: Case study: public, fixed Codex CLI and Claude Code bugs whose class Tide prevents or makes replayable
description:
## Why
The owner said on 2026-11-17: "we should def. try to find bugs in codex and claude code that tide solves". tide-lead offered 1 (a post-alpha research bead) or 2 (before the alpha). He answered "you decide", relayed by tide-desk, which chose 1. The case study shows real bugs, in the very tools that build Tide, whose class Tide prevents or makes replayable. It's launch and paper follow-up material, and a natural hook for Felipe Coury (@fcoury, Codex CLI).

## Rules
- Only public, already-fixed issues and PRs: Codex CLI (open-source Rust) and Claude Code's public issue tracker. No hunting for new vulnerabilities, no running exploits against the products, no undisclosed holes.
- Framing: a gift to the Codex and Claude Code teams ("here's how this bug class becomes impossible or replayable"), never a gotcha. No claim stronger than its source. Each bug links to its issue or PR and its fix.
- Agents draft the research. Anything public goes out through the owner.

## Scope
1. Survey fixed issues in those classes:
   - concurrency races, ordering bugs and flaky behavior (Tide's simulator plus replay);
   - sandbox or permission escapes and unintended network or filesystem reach (capabilities, RUN-3);
   - review-invisible authority growth (the trust diff);
   - nondeterminism that blocked reproduction (replay).
2. For each candidate, state the mechanism, which Tide rule or feature addresses it (cite design/ and conformance/rules.md), and the limits: what Tide wouldn't catch, and whether the code could even be written in Tide's v0 subset.
3. Write up 5-10 strong cases, not a long list, and say where Tide doesn't help.

## Acceptance
A research note in research/ with linked sources, each case's mechanism and the Tide rule that addresses it, plus an honest limits section, reviewed under the Merge Rule for docs. Nothing is posted by an agent.

Post-alpha: blocked by fx-qlek.

title: Adopt BeautifulRust's clippy lints and Rust guidance for Tide's own crates
description:
## Why
Owner, 2026-11-17: "wanna create a bead to apply this later? not very important ofc", about https://github.com/morganlinton/BeautifulRust (MIT; 1.9k stars).

BeautifulRust ships:
- a drop-in clippy config (lints/lints.toml, lints/clippy.toml), with a check crate that proves each lint fires;
- agent skills (rust-best-practices, rust-review), distilled from the Rust API Guidelines, Effective Rust, and Google's and Microsoft's Rust guides.

Tide's crates are agent-written, so these lints catch the shortcuts agents take: unwrap outside tests, unsafe without a SAFETY comment, #[allow] without a reason, lossy `as` casts, missing # Errors and # Panics docs.

## Scope
- Pin a BeautifulRust commit.

title: Define the Ferox full-fidelity syntax trivia and comment-preservation model for CST, formatter, and docs
description: The specs now assume full-fidelity syntax, conservative formatter recovery, doc-comment attachment, and comment/trivia preservation, but the queue does not yet track the exact model that parser and formatter work should implement. This task should define how Ferox represents trivia, comments, and doc comments in the concrete syntax tree so later formatter, docs, and safe rewrite tooling can rely on one durable source-preserving model.
design: Primary question: what full-fidelity syntax model should Ferox use so parsing, formatting, documentation, and later refactors preserve source meaning and source-adjacent structure without inventing ad hoc side channels? Define: 1. whether trivia is token-attached, node-attached, or stored in a separate full-fidelity layer; 2. how line comments, block comments if any, and doc comments are tokenized and attached; 3. what syntax tree invariants the formatter and parser recovery logic may rely on; 4. what stays intentionally out of scope for the first parser slice.
acceptance_criteria: Done means this task clearly answers: how comments and trivia are represented; how doc comments attach to declarations; what parser/formatter invariants the CST guarantees; and what validation/logging expectations apply. Include worked examples for preserved comments and doc comments, rejected alternative models, unit/corpus/e2e validation expectations, and tracing requirements for trivia-preserving parsing and formatting decisions.
notes: Decision: Ferox should use one full-fidelity CST model that preserves comments, doc comments, whitespace, and other trivia in source order rather than discarding them into side tables. AST/lowered views may omit trivia, but formatter, documentation generation, and later structural rewrites should all derive from this same source-preserving CST. Conservative recovery must preserve original text for uncertain regions.

title: Order sink output against an inherited child's stdout/stderr; spell stdout-to-stderr redirection
description:
## Why

`Stdio::inherit()` (the default for `status()` and `spawn()`) hands a child file descriptors 1 and
2 directly, while Tide's `out` and `err` sinks go through a process-wide buffer that a writer
thread drains (SINK-5). So `println!("building"); cmd.status()?;` can print the child's output
before "building", which Rust never does. Separately, Rust's `.stdout(io::stderr())` idiom lost its
spelling when fx-obr dropped `From<io::Stdout>`/`From<io::Stderr>` for `Stdio`, and nothing names a
replacement. Found by round 68 (N5) while reviewing fx-obr; the ordering gap predates that change.

## Evidence

- `design/03-authority-concurrency.md` §1.1 `Stdio` note; §2.4 SINK-1, SINK-4, SINK-5.
- `design/reference.md` 6.5; `design/reference-companion.md` 20.
- `reviews/round68-consistency.md` N5.

## Scope

In scope: decide how sink output and an inherited child's output are ordered (for example, spawn
flushes the task's `out` and `err` buffers and waits for the writer first), including inside
`join`/`par_*` branch buffers (SINK-4) and under simulation; decide whether a child's stdout can be
redirected to the parent's stderr and how to spell it. State both in 03 and the reference pair.

Out of scope: other process semantics under simulation.

## Acceptance

- 03 decides both points with reasoning; companion 20 (or the core, within D14's budget) states them.
- A review round in `reviews/` finds no contradiction among 03, the reference pair, and the SINK rules.

## Notes

Prefer Rust's observable behavior (D18). Docs-only: review rounds, not converge.
close_reason: SINK-4 orders sink output before a child on the process's descriptors; SINK-5 discards unwritable records; Stdio regains From<io::Stdout/Stderr>; rounds 76-79 clean (Codex approve, round 79)

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Decisions (03 SINK-4, SINK-5, §1.1 Stdio note; companion 20):
- Order: when Command's spawn/status/output starts a child whose stdout or stderr is the process's own (inherit, the spawn/status default, or io::stdout()/io::stderr()), it first waits until the writer has written every earlier sink record (or dropped it where SINK-5 allows); branch records count once their join appends them. Backpressure, not suspension; the simulator needs none (SINK-6). SINK-5 adds: a record that cannot be written to stderr is discarded, so the wait always ends. Rejected: piping the child through the writer thread (round 68 N5's alternative): extra copies and changes the child's isatty view; unconditional wait (blocks output() needlessly).
- Redirection: restore Rust's From<io::Stdout>/From<io::Stderr> for Stdio (reverses fx-obr's drop): they name fds 1 and 2, exactly as inherit() does, so they grant nothing new, and SINK-4 removes the ordering hazard that motivated the drop. .stdout(io::stderr()) ports unchanged (D18). Cost: under root.log.to_file, io::stderr() as a sink writes to the file, but as a Stdio it is fd 2.
- Simulation: sim.world.proc model output placement stays out of scope (bead).
Core unchanged (24,999).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Wording update after rounds 77-78: SINK-5 says out/err are never dropped under load, and any record (other than the closed-stdout exit-141 case) that cannot be written to its destination is discarded, so SINK-4's wait always ends; SINK-4 counts a branch's records as emitted when the outermost join appends them to its task's output.

title: Regression test: backstop on a static pointing at an upstream fn
description:
## Why

fx-kw8.4's round 2 (reviews/fx-kw8.4-r2-opus.md, fix 1) fixed a driver ICE: a static whose value points at an upstream non-generic function, such as `pub static LOWER: fn(&str) -> String = str::to_lowercase;`, made the backstop ask `items_of_instance` for an item rustc links rather than instantiates, which has no MIR (exit 101). The fix holds (`uses` runs only on collected mono items), but no checked-in test protects it; the narrow Codex re-check (reviews/fx-kw8.4-r4-codex.md) asked for one.

## Acceptance

- A driver test in `crates/tide-admit/tests/driver.rs` checks that program with the minimal Tide std the backstop tests build (`tide_std()`), in normal and `--tide-test-backstop` mode, and expects exit 0 with no diagnostics.
- `cargo test --workspace` exits 0.
close_reason: Driver test the_backstop_skips_upstream_functions_a_static_points_at checks LOWER = str::to_lowercase in normal and --tide-test-backstop mode, exit 0, empty stderr; it fails with round 2's ICE when the pre-fix traversal is restored (r1 Opus). tide_std takes a per-test directory. cargo test --workspace exit 0. Reviews r1 Opus clean, r1 Codex approve.

title: #![no_std] hides Tide's std from tide-admit, switching off Pure
description:
## Why

`Crates::new` (`crates/tide-admit/src/crates.rs`, `injected_std`) takes Tide's std to be the crate
behind the `extern crate std` that rustc's std injection adds. A candidate's `#![no_std]` changes
that injection to `core`, and an explicit `extern crate std;` still links the operator's Tide std.
`Crates::tide_std()` is then `None`, so (a) the walk builds no `Pure` decision (`Walk::new`), which
switches off every rule that needs one (GLOBAL-1 statics, AFREE-1/2, LOCK-1/4, PAR-4..7, PURE-1),
and (b) Tide's std's items get `Role::Other`, so each use is FX0520 and none of its re-exports
count as exported. Found by Codex in fx-kw8.8 round 1 (`reviews/fx-kw8.8-r1-codex.md`, B1);
fx-kw8.8 moved only FX0512's switch to the operator's `--tide-std`.

Evidence: `conformance/cases/authority/root_main_no_std.rs` shows (b): `fn main() {}` under
`#![no_std]` + `extern crate std;` gets FX0520 for `impl Termination for ()`. Whether (a) admits a
crate that the injected-std build rejects (for example a core-only non-`Pure` `static`, or a
`#[pure]` fn over a core type with interior mutability) is not yet shown.

## Scope

Decide and enforce how a candidate's `#![no_std]` (and `#![no_core]`, already unstable) is treated:
either reject it (it is not part of the Tide surface; check `design/reference.md` and D18's
allowlist before choosing, and pick the FX code the design gives or record the choice) or identify
Tide's std from the operator's `--tide-std` artifact rather than from the candidate's std injection.
Record the decision and its reason on this bead.

## Acceptance

A conformance case with `#![no_std]` + `extern crate std;` that defines something the injected-std
build rejects for `Pure` (or the attribute itself, if rejected) gets the same verdict as without
`#![no_std]`; `conformance/run.sh` exits 0 and `cargo test --workspace` passes.
close_reason: done

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Decision (agent, technical): reject `#![no_std]` under the operator's --tide-std as FX0520 (ADMIT-1), rather than identify Tide's std from the --tide-std artifact. Reason: identification alone would still leave a core-only `#![no_std]` crate (no `extern crate std`) with no Pure decision, so the Pure rules would stay off; rejecting keeps Tide's std the injected std that Crates::tide_std and the rules key on, as `#![no_main]` is already rejected (FX0512). `#![no_core]` is an unstable feature, already closed by -Zallow-features= (ADMIT-2). Recorded in 03 ADMIT-1's list and rules.md's ADMIT-1 row.

Cases: admit_no_std (active cfg_attr + extern crate std), root_main_no_std and admit_crate_identity marked; driver test asserts plain #![no_std] rejection with no artifact and that an inactive cfg_attr(any(), no_std) is admitted. title: Enforce FX0506: no code calls main (ROOT-5)
description:
## Why

ROOT-5 (`design/03-authority-concurrency.md` §2.1): no code calls `main` or uses it as a value
(`FX0506`), so a test cannot mint a real `Root` through it. tide-admit does not decide FX0506 yet
(`conformance/cases/authority/root_main_called.rs` is AWAITS CHECKER). Once fx-kw8.9 builds and
runs test executables, a `#[test]` that calls the crate-root `main` that `#[tide::main]` generates
mints a real `Root` inside a test, which breaks RUN-1's sandbox guarantee. Found by the fx-nkv.1
worker (2026-11-01).

## Scope

Enforce ROOT-5 in `crates/tide-admit` under `FX0506`: any call of, or reference to, the binary's
`main` (including through a path, a re-export, or a function pointer) outside the toolchain's own
entry wiring. Keep the generated entry point and the test harness admitted.

## Acceptance

`conformance/cases/authority/root_main_called.rs` PASSes (no longer AWAITS CHECKER for FX0506),
with a case that takes `main` as a value; `conformance/run.sh` exits 0 and
`cargo test --workspace` passes.
close_reason: done

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: From fx-nkv.1's worker (2026-11-01, r3 probe): under --test a library crate is an executable crate, so a library's crate-root #[tide::main] fn main is trusted there (lib mode reports FX0520 for its __rt::enter call; --test admits it). FX0506 must cover any generated crate-root main, a library's under --test included; otherwise fx-kw8.9 must run the library-mode check before building tests.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Done in 0eb9845 (base 5661fa8). FX0506: tide-admit reports every HIR path that resolves to the crate-root fn main of an executable crate (binary, or any crate under --test; the harness's own main excluded), with no toolchain-span exemption, since the entry wiring never names main but a #[test] on it calls it. Crates owns that main (is_main) and derives the #[tide::main] entry expansion from it, replacing entry_expansion. Cases: root_main_called (call, value, import, test call) PASSes; new root_main_called_library (library under --test) and root_main_test (#[cfg_attr(test, test)] on main). Reviews: r1 Opus clean (nits fixed), r1 Codex request_changes (test-descriptor bypass via generated_by_toolchain; fixed, regression root_main_test FAILs with the exemption restored), r2 Opus clean, r3 Codex approve. Decision (C1/C2, both reviewers concur): under --test a library's plain crate-root fn main helper, or a crate-root #[test] fn main, is FX0506 though it mints nothing; accepted as safe-side and literal ROOT-5, renaming avoids it. Checks on 0eb9845's tree: cargo test --workspace exit 0; conformance/run.sh exit 0 (193 PASS, no FAIL).

title: Stable item identity and definition hashes in tide-admit
description:
## Why

Every seal hash (SEAL-2, `design/04-contracts.md:1265-1280`) and §11's spec-closure
hash (`04:1200-1213`) identify items by stable ID and abstract the names hashed text
references, so a rename changes nothing while an edit to a referenced definition does.
fx-kw8.10 gives public items an identity for the authority artifact; seals also need
private items, impl methods by qualified path (`<Entry as PartialEq>::eq`), and tests,
per configuration. This slice builds the one identity and definition-hash owner.

## Evidence

- `design/01-design.md:894` (D14): definitions are content-hashed; symbols have stable IDs.
- `design/04-contracts.md:1247-1280`: SEAL-1 entries by stable ID; SEAL-2's resolution
  and dependency rules (std by toolchain version, dependencies by locked content hash).
- The stable-ID and cycle decisions recorded by fx-zr3.
- fx-kw8.10's public-item identity in `crates/tide-admit/`.

## Scope

In scope: `crates/tide-admit/`: stable IDs for every item the seal can name; a
definition hash per item and configuration that records what each path, method call,
operator, and associated-type projection resolves to, by stable ID and content hash,
not by name; cycles hashed as fx-zr3 decides; std hashed by toolchain
version, dependencies by locked content hash. Extend fx-kw8.10's identity rather than
adding a second one.

Out of scope: clause normalization (fx-kw8.16); seal files and FX0920.

## Acceptance

- Tests in `crates/tide-admit/tests/` show: renaming a referenced item leaves the
  referencing item's hash unchanged; editing it changes the hash; a new impl or import
  that changes which item a call selects changes it; a doc-comment or formatting edit
  changes nothing; mutually recursive functions hash deterministically.
- fx-kw8.10's artifact uses the same identity.

## Verification

- `cargo test --workspace` exits 0.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if fx-zr3's decisions do not cover a case this slice meets; record it there rather than deciding a second owner here.
- Stop if verification fails twice for the same reason after a reasonable fix attempt.

title: Clause normalization and spec-closure hashes in tide-admit
description:
## Why

An interface seal entry fixes a function's contract through §11's spec-closure hash

title: Seal whole types and traits with the impls that apply
description:
## Why

Types, traits, and constants are always sealed whole (SEAL-2,
`design/04-contracts.md:1285-1310`): a whole type fixes its fields, variants,
generics, bounds, attributes, derives, and every impl in the crate that applies to

This needs trait selection and is the hardest SEAL-2 part.

## Evidence

## Scope

In scope: `crates/tide-admit/`: whole entries for structs, enums, aliases,
constants, and traits; the applies-to relation, counting an impl as applying wherever
trait selection cannot rule it out; private inherent methods fixed; new trait impls

title: Explain structural Pure failures with one witness path
description:
## Why

Tide rejects a payload that reaches authority, but its diagnostic identifies only the outer and terminal types. An agent repairing a nested struct must rediscover which field carries the authority. `NotPure` stores `part` and `why`, and `Pure::walk` discards the edges traversed (`/home/lucca/pjs/lab/tide/crates/tide-admit/src/pure.rs:252–308,348–423`, Tide `b7250d371d2c3ca2de09036960f41042417ddd41`). D14 already requires exact and related spans for useful diagnostics (`design/01-design.md:870–874`). Earlier research proposed authority witness call paths (`research/12-newcomer-sweep.md:347–357`); this is a bounded structural implementation task, not a new policy or call-graph feature.

Zed records origins as data and renders them when a rejection needs its derivation (`/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/tide-zed-research-work/zed/crates/zedc-check/src/check/mod.rs:558–608`, Zed `a1917a0cca884f621956281ef95a3e3405c61e7b`). **Inference:** a single structural witness is the smallest useful adaptation for Tide; a general derivation engine is unnecessary.

## Evidence

- Tide `crates/tide-admit/src/pure.rs:252–308`: the current failure payload and terminal-type message.

title: Check FX diagnostic stability under harmless source edits
description:
## Why

An agent should not receive a different FX reason or lose a diagnostic because it moved an independent item or inserted a comment. Tide asserts exact diagnostics for fixed fixtures and sorts/deduplicates them, but the inspected tests do not compare harmless transformations of the same program (`/home/lucca/pjs/lab/tide/crates/tide-admit/tests/driver.rs:8–42,74–95,340–391`; `crates/tide-admit/src/diag.rs:118–184`, Tide `b7250d371d2c3ca2de09036960f41042417ddd41`). D14 expects stable codes and exact spans (`design/01-design.md:870–874`).

Zed compares printed types and diagnostics after repeated checks, unrelated edits and item permutations, using item-relative offsets (`/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/tide-zed-research-work/zed/tests/steps/l01_29_diagnostics/stable.rs:1–6,124–190`; `order.rs:1–8`, Zed `a1917a0cca884f621956281ef95a3e3405c61e7b`). **Inference:** a small transformation matrix at Tide's public driver boundary can catch traversal-order and span-mapping mistakes without adopting Zed's parser or source model.

## Evidence

- Tide `crates/tide-admit/src/diag.rs:118–184`: identity/deduplication and source-order emission.
- Tide `crates/tide-admit/tests/driver.rs:8–42`: existing subprocess helper and FX extraction.
- Tide `crates/tide-admit/tests/driver.rs:340–391`: exact location assertions for backstop diagnostics, a useful existing surface.
- Tide `conformance/README.md:110–119`: fixed-fixture line/code comparisons; neither a transformation matrix nor a diagnostic-count contract.
- Zed `tests/steps/l01_29_diagnostics/order.rs:1–8,21–22`: source-relative comparison and fixed shuffle seed.
- Zed `tests/steps/l01_29_diagnostics/stable.rs:124–190`: fresh/repeated checks, comment and unrelated binding insertion.
- Existing-work check: `br --no-db` searches for `diagnostic`, `span`, `metamorphic` and `cache`; read `fx-kw8`, `fx-u65`, `fx-gcs`, `fx-upy`. `fx-u65` owns rule completeness and `fx-upy` ports the corpus runner. Neither owns this invariant. This task extends `fx-kw8` through its existing integration tests.

## Scope

In: a few deliberately small Rust fixtures and variants in `crates/tide-admit/tests/driver.rs` (or one local test module if useful). Select independent top-level items with no source-order-sensitive macros/attributes. Exercise a normal walk rejection and a backstop rejection if both can be reached using existing helpers. Repeat fresh driver invocations, reverse the independent items, insert blank/comment lines, and add an unrelated accepted item. Include an accepted control.

Compare diagnostics by owning fixture block, mapped start location, FX code, severity and message, retaining multiplicity. Compare known short-format fields rather than all rustc output. Build the source and its location mapping from the same small block list; do not add a Rust parser. Any confirmed defect these tests expose in the current diagnostic owner is in scope to fix narrowly.

Out: arbitrary corpus rewriting, changing the conformance format or `run.sh`, adding JSON/NDJSON support, compiler inference changes, new FX rules, benchmarking, a generalized mutation framework, new dependencies, and held-out trial inputs. Rejected compilations are not cache hits; do not present repeated failures as cache-reuse proof.

## Acceptance

- Each rejected variant returns rejection and the same nonempty diagnostic multiset as its original after applying the known location mapping; no diagnostic disappears or changes reason/code/severity. Source order may change presentation order.
- The accepted control remains accepted after the same harmless transformations.
- The comparison demonstrably fails on a missing diagnostic, duplicate diagnostic, changed FX code or wrong mapped line/column. A small comparison self-check is enough; no compiler mutants need be committed.
- Cheapest falsifier: move two independent rejecting functions and insert a comment above one. The test fails if any normalized diagnostic changes or if it compares zero expected diagnostics.

## Verification

`cargo test -p tide-admit --test driver` must pass on the pinned toolchain under Tide's scheduling rules (`nice -n 19`, `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4`, no active quiet window). A test-only change needs no conformance rebuild. If it exposes a production defect, run checks for that changed owner and the affected rule's cases. Close subprocess stdin and bound waits. This research ran no builds or suites.

Review and landing follow `GOVERNANCE.md`'s Merge Rule; any full suite runs through the coordinator's `heavy.sh` slot.

## Stop Conditions

If a transformation changes Rust name resolution, cfg behavior, reachability or program semantics, replace that fixture/transform rather than redefine language behavior. Reconcile materially changed driver/test APIs before writing. Report a discovered defect requiring a new diagnostic protocol or acceptance-policy change instead of expanding this task. Never normalize away codes, severity, meaningful message text, duplicate records or the location field being tested.

## Maintenance Notes

Keep this a fixed, bounded matrix over hand-selected source blocks. Reuse the existing subprocess boundary and comparison conventions; sharing one small local helper is sufficient. Avoid snapshots of unowned rustc prose and broad shuffle coverage with no distinct failure target. If the witness-path task lands first, the diagnostic text used here includes that path naturally; there is no logical dependency, but shared edits should land sequentially.

- Source: the Zed comparison of 2026-11-11 (Zed `a1917a0`, Tide `b7250d3`), requested by the owner; the research report is not in the repository.

title: tide-admit owns every rustc invocation
description:
## Why

D18: the driver owns every rustc invocation. It passes `-Zallow-features=`, adds no user-controlled
`--extern`, `-L`, `--sysroot`, `--cfg`, or semantic `-C` flags, runs no build scripts or proc macros
for Tide crates except the toolchain's, injects Tide's std with `--extern std=`, and keeps its own
content-addressed cache. The spike's `spikes/d18/admit/scripts/tide-rustc` is the prototype gate.
Parent epic has the context.

## Scope

In scope: the invocation layer in `crates/`, its tests, and the RUN-2 build-isolation cases that
need no sandbox (rejected `include_*!`, `env!`, `#[path]`, ignored `RUSTFLAGS`, `RUSTC_WRAPPER`,
`.cargo/config.toml`, `rust-toolchain.toml`; `build.rs` is FX0915). Out of scope: the OS sandbox
and the test harness (RUN-3 onward).

## Acceptance

- A crate cannot change the flags rustc receives; each RUN-2 case in scope passes.

## Verification

- `cargo test --workspace` and `conformance/run.sh` exit 0; converge, then the review loop.

title: Mono-item backstop for denied impls in tide-admit
description:
## Why

fx-kw8.1's HIR walk closes admission routes one at a time: review rounds 2–5
(`reviews/fx-kw8.1-r2..r5-opus.md`) each found another route to a denied impl
through obligations, fn-item where-clauses, or `main`'s `Termination` bound. Every one of
them ends in a few denied impls (core's `impl<F: FnPtr> Debug/Hash/PartialOrd/Ord/Pointer
for F`, `impl Default for RandomState`, and the array `From` impls of `HashMap`/`HashSet`).
All of these are generic or `#[inline]`, so an instance that can run is among the local crate's
mono items however the code reached it. A check over mono items would catch the routes
the walk has not found yet.

## Design (from round 5, not built)

- In `after_analysis`, which runs only when rustc and the walk found no errors, call
  `tcx.collect_and_partition_mono_items(())`. For each `MonoItem::Fn` that is a method of a
  non-local trait impl, build the impl key as `admit_impl` does. Reject only on an explicit
  `Deny` or an ungranted `Unsafe` rule. Unlisted keys do not count, because std's internals
  instantiate unlisted impls.
- Report at the nearest local mono item: walk `mentioned_items` back from the instance, and
  only when something is rejected. Failing that, report at the crate root and name the
  instance.
- Record in D18/ADMIT-1 that this part of the gate runs after type checking.

## Open points

- Forcing mono collection in `--emit metadata` builds costs time, and post-mono const errors
  then appear in check builds.
- `-Zshare-generics` is on by default at opt-level 0. A downstream crate can link an upstream
  instance instead of making its own. `-Zshare-generics=no` would need an ADMIT-2 line.
- In a lib, the roots are only the reachable non-generic items.
- Testing: once the walk is right, no program reaches the backstop alone. Pick one: a test
  switch that disables the walk's obligation step, or a probe corpus kept as evidence.

## Acceptance

- With the walk's obligation step disabled, the backstop alone rejects each of fx-kw8.1's
  r2–r5 hole probes with FX0520 at a local span. With the walk enabled, the diagnostics are
  the same as before.
- D18/ADMIT-1 state when the backstop runs; `cargo test --workspace` and
  `conformance/run.sh` exit 0.
close_reason: Backstop in tide-admit (walk/mono.rs, after analysis): denied/ungranted impl instances FX0520 and Pure where-clauses at uses, over rustc's lazily collected mono items with build-equivalent roots (reachable_non_generics override) and -Zshare-generics=no. With --tide-test-backstop the backstop alone rejects every fx-kw8.1 r2-r5 route at a local span (tests/driver.rs) and the fx-kw8.2 Pure routes that have instances; with the walk on, diagnostics unchanged (conformance 181 PASS/28 AWAITS, exit 0; cargo test --workspace exit 0). ADMIT-1, ADMIT-2, D18 record when it runs. Reviews r1 (Opus+Codex), r2-r3 Opus (r3 clean), r4 Codex approve.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Scope extension from fx-kw8.2 (decision, 2026-10-21): fx-kw8.2's review rounds 4–7 kept finding routes where rustc discharges a local item's `X: Pure` clause through std's blanket impl without selecting a checked impl: Drop-impl bounds, impl-item where-clauses, opaque associated-type bounds, GAT where-clauses named in generic args, and constructors used as values. Each was closed in the HIR walk (reviews/fx-kw8.2-r4..r7-opus.md; r6 has a 29-row discharge-site table). The route-independent closure is this bead's backstop: for every local mono item, instantiate its predicates and its parents' (impl and trait) and decide their `Pure` part with pure.rs. That catches any remaining route in reachable code. Same open points as above: lib roots, share-generics, cost, and how to test something the walk already covers.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Decisions, 2026-10-31 (agent; technical, per AGENTS.md Decisions):

- Mechanism: `crates/tide-admit/src/walk/mono.rs`, run from `after_analysis` (rustc's analysis raises fatal on any earlier error, so it runs only when rustc and the walk found none). rustc's collector (`collect_and_partition_mono_items`) runs eagerly (`-Clink-dead-code`): a metadata-only build exports no symbols, so lazy collection has no library roots (`rustc_codegen_ssa/src/back/symbol_export.rs:55`). Eager collection also instantiates provided methods, const values, and drop glue that never run (round 1, both reviewers), so the backstop keeps only items reachable from local non-generic fns, local statics, and the `start` instance through `items_of_instance(UsedItems)` and static-initializer pointers.
- `-Zshare-generics=no`: the crate instantiates upstream generics itself (except `#[inline(never)]` ones an upstream crate made), so their instances are among its mono items. Both flags are recorded in ADMIT-2.
- FX0520: a non-local trait impl method whose `impl_key` an explicit Deny rule or an ungranted Unsafe rule matches; unlisted keys do not count. Reported at the nearest local users (BFS back through non-local users; `start` stands for `main`), else the crate root.
- Pure (scope extension): for live items of the local crate, Tide's std, or other Tide crates, `use_generic` plus the trait method's own clauses at rebased args, in a fully monomorphized environment; decided once, reported only at uses. Roots' clauses are their callers' preconditions, so an uncalled root is not checked.
- Test switch: `--tide-test-backstop` skips the walk's `obligation` and `pure_obligation`. Kept as an operator-trusted flag (operators already choose grants; the cache key records it) rather than a debug-only build, so `cargo test` exercises the shipped binary.
- Not covered: generic-only code with no instance in the crate (the walk owns it; a downstream crate's backstop sees its instances); `std::path::absolute` from r2 was a missing path rule, not an impl route.
- Constraint: the backstop needs optimized MIR for every upstream generic it reaches. A dependency checked by tide-admit alone is a metadata-only rmeta without MIR, and collection would stop with rustc's NoOptimizedMir fatal; dependencies must be full rlibs (as the stub std is) until multi-crate builds are designed.
- Cost: conformance corpus 2m18s before the roots fix, 2m22s after (209 cases, 4 driver runs each); round 1 measured 1.6x wall time on a 600-line library before per-use deciding was removed.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Correction, 2026-10-31, after review round 2 (reviews/fx-kw8.4-r2-opus.md): the earlier decisions comment is stale on collection. Eager collection (`-Clink-dead-code`) is gone: rustc's collector raised post-monomorphization errors (a provided method's failing `const` assert) in code that never runs, which no root filter can stop. The driver now collects lazily and overrides the `reachable_non_generics` query with `rustc_codegen_ssa::back::symbol_export::reachable_non_generics_helper` (the helper rustc exposes for Miri), so a metadata check has a full build's roots: what a library exports (Rust-level threshold), statics, and the entry point; a bin or `--test` build checks what its entry reaches. Metadata output is unchanged (round 3 checked the encoder). Every collected item is live; ADMIT-2 records one added flag, `-Zshare-generics=no`. What a library's build does not export (generics, `#[inline]` functions, closures returned uncalled) is checked in the crates that instantiate them. Round 3 was clean; conformance takes 2m25s (2m18s at the first candidate).

title: FX0915 finds build.rs only beside src/ entries
description:
## Why

D13 and `design/reference.md` §12.4 ("No `build.rs`") make a package build script `FX0915`. tide-admit finds the package root by a heuristic: when the entry file's directory is named `src`, its parent is the package; otherwise the entry's own directory is (`crates/tide-admit/src/invocation.rs`, the `lexical_package` computation in `run()`, then `package.join("build.rs")`). An entry at `pkg/src/bin/tool.rs` or `pkg/tests/t.rs` therefore misses `pkg/build.rs`, so a package with a build script gets no FX0915. The driver never runs the script, so nothing executes; the gap is a missing verdict. Found in fx-kw8.3 review rounds 1 and 5 (`reviews/fx-kw8.3-r1-opus.md` N9, `reviews/fx-kw8.3-r5-opus.md`).

## Evidence

- `crates/tide-admit/src/invocation.rs`, `run()`: `lexical_package` takes the parent only when the entry's directory is named `src`, and FX0915 checks `package.join("build.rs")`.
- `design/reference.md` §12.4: the manifest is `tide.toml` (provisional name and keys), with no `build` key.
- `README.md` (the tide-admit section) documents the current rule: "The source directory is the entry's parent; when it is named `src`, its parent is the package directory."

## Scope

In scope:
- Package-root detection in `crates/tide-admit/src/invocation.rs`, its tests in `crates/tide-admit/tests/invocation.rs`, and the README sentence above.

Out of scope:
- Parsing `tide.toml` or `Cargo.toml` keys; a package manager.
- The snapshot root: the source directory stays the entry's parent, and only the FX0915 lookup and the out-of-package checks use the package root.
- Running anything.

## Acceptance

- A package with `build.rs` at its root gets FX0915 (exit 1) when the entry is `src/lib.rs`, `src/main.rs`, `src/bin/<x>.rs`, or `tests/<x>.rs`, and nothing reads or runs the script.
- Single-file roots (an entry whose directory has no package marker) behave as today.

## Implementation Notes

1. Pick the marker: the nearest ancestor of the entry, within a bounded walk, that holds `tide.toml` or `Cargo.toml`, falling back to today's `src` rule when none is found. Record the choice and why on this bead and in the README.
2. Keep the existing symlink and containment checks (the package path must not traverse a directory symlink; output must sit outside the package) working with the new root.
3. Add the four entry shapes to `build_scripts_are_rejected_without_running` in `crates/tide-admit/tests/invocation.rs`.

## Verification

- `timeout 1200 cargo test --workspace < /dev/null` exits 0.
- `timeout 1800 conformance/run.sh < /dev/null` exits 0 with 0 FAIL.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if choosing the marker needs an owner decision on the manifest's name. `design/reference.md` calls `tide.toml` provisional; ask only if the design changes it.
- Stop if the walk would need to read files outside the entry's ancestors.

## Maintenance Notes

- Finish through converge, then the GOVERNANCE.md review loop.

title: Candidate-controlled inputs give exit 2 instead of a verdict
description:
## Why

RUN-2 says a symbolic link or path that leaves the candidate tree "reads as missing", and exit 2 is tide-admit's setup-error class: `conformance/run.sh` treats a driver exit above 1 as "the driver crashed". fx-kw8.3 fixed this for unreferenced snapshot entries. These candidate-controlled inputs still turn a check into exit 2 instead of a verdict (exit 1), or into reading as missing:
- an unreadable subdirectory under the source directory (`fs::read_dir(dir)?` in `Sources::snapshot`'s `walk`);
- an entry file that is not valid UTF-8, or an entry symlink that resolves outside the source directory ("candidate source is not admitted");
- an `--out-dir` whose missing part contains `..` (`destination()`). This one is operator input, so it is lower priority.
Found in `reviews/fx-kw8.3-r3-opus.md`, `r5`, and `r6`.

## Evidence

- `crates/tide-admit/src/invocation.rs`, `Sources::snapshot`: `fs::read_dir(dir)?` aborts the snapshot.
- `crates/tide-admit/src/invocation.rs`, `run()`: `return Err("candidate source is not admitted".into())`, which exits 2.
- `crates/tide-admit/src/invocation.rs`, `destination()`.
- `crates/tide-admit/tests/invocation.rs`, `candidate_content_gets_rustc_diagnostics_and_every_verdict`: the existing test for unreferenced dangling or non-UTF-8 entries.

## Scope

In scope:
- `crates/tide-admit/src/invocation.rs` (snapshot walk, entry admission, `destination`) and its tests.

Out of scope:
- The loader's authorization rules: what the snapshot serves must not grow.
- The cache key layout, except as needed to record a skipped entry.

## Acceptance

- An unreadable subdirectory reads as missing: the crate is checked, and a module in it gets rustc's E0583 (exit 1).
- A non-UTF-8 entry, or an entry symlink leaving the source directory, gets a verdict (exit 1, a short-format error naming the entry) and never discloses the target's bytes.
- `--out-dir` with `..` in a missing component either works or fails with a clear setup error; record which on this bead.

## Implementation Notes

1. Write a failing test for each input first, in `crates/tide-admit/tests/invocation.rs`.
2. Skip unreadable directories the way fx-kw8.3 skips unreadable files.
3. Report entry failures as a rejection (exit 1). Do not let them reach rustc's parse fallback, which reopens paths directly after a loader error on this pin (`rustc_parse/src/lib.rs` around line 118).

## Verification

- `timeout 1200 cargo test --workspace < /dev/null` exits 0.
- `timeout 1800 conformance/run.sh < /dev/null` exits 0 with 0 FAIL.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if a fix would let the loader serve any path outside the snapshot.

## Maintenance Notes

- Finish through converge, then the GOVERNANCE.md review loop.

title: rustc ICE reports can be written into the candidate tree
description:
## Why

RUN-2 allows the toolchain to write only its artifact cache and the run's output directory. tide-admit runs rustc with an empty environment (fx-kw8.3). On this nightly, a compiler crash then writes `rustc-ice-<time>-<pid>.txt` to the process's current directory (`rustc_driver_impl/src/lib.rs:1404-1428`: `RUSTC_ICE` unset gives `-Zmetrics-dir`, else `current_dir()`), and that directory may be inside the candidate tree. fx-kw8.3 review round 3 found such a file in the repository, left by a seeded crash (`reviews/fx-kw8.3-r3-opus.md`). A candidate that can trigger an ICE can make the gate write into its own tree, and the report holds compiler internals.

## Evidence

- `/home/lucca/.rustup/toolchains/nightly-2026-08-09-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/lib/rustlib/rustc-src/rust/compiler/rustc_driver_impl/src/lib.rs:1404-1428`: ICE path selection; `RUSTC_ICE=0` opts out.
- `crates/tide-admit/src/invocation.rs`, `run()`: the top-level re-exec with `env_clear()` whenever the environment is non-empty, and the `--tide-compile` child, also spawned with `env_clear()`.

## Scope

In scope:
- Where the compile child's crash reports go, in `crates/tide-admit/src/invocation.rs`, plus one test.

Out of scope:
- The OS build sandbox (Landlock/seccomp), which is later work.
- Changing the cleared environment for anything other than this one variable or directory.

## Acceptance

- When rustc ICEs under tide-admit, no file appears outside the output directory's `.tide-cache`. The ICE either goes nowhere (`RUSTC_ICE=0`) or into the staging directory, which is removed on failure.
- The driver still exits non-zero with rustc's ICE message on stderr.

## Implementation Notes

1. Pitfall: `run()` re-execs with a cleared environment whenever any variable is set. Simply adding `RUSTC_ICE=0` to the child makes the child re-exec and drop it. Either let the worker mode keep exactly that variable, or pass `-Zmetrics-dir=<staging dir>` among the driver-built rustc arguments (no env change; check that it also accepts the ICE path on this pin).
2. Test: force an ICE with a seeded change if no stable trigger exists. Use `-Ztreat-err-as-bug` only if the fixed interface can reach it in a test-only path. Otherwise verify by reading the code path and record why.

## Verification

- `timeout 1200 cargo test --workspace < /dev/null` exits 0.
- `timeout 1800 conformance/run.sh < /dev/null` exits 0 with 0 FAIL.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the fix needs a user-controlled rustc flag: ADMIT-2 forbids them.

## Maintenance Notes

- Finish through converge, then the GOVERNANCE.md review loop.
close_reason: done

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Done. The clean process's whole environment is RUSTC_ICE=0: run() re-execs unless the environment is exactly that (an empty one too), both spawns set it, and rustc's ICE hook is installed only after that normalization (moved from main.rs), so a crash in the compiler or a panic before compilation writes no rustc-ice file; the crash message still goes to stderr and the exit code passes through. Test-only flag --tide-test-ice seeds a compiler panic (in the cache key). The driver never executes candidate output. All edits are uncommitted; the bead remains in progress.

## Changes

- `crates/tide-admit/src/invocation.rs`: fixed link/profile inputs, admission before codegen, executable publication/cleanup, linker fingerprints, uncached unsafe-granted links.
- `crates/tide-admit/src/main.rs`: command and isolation documentation.
- `crates/tide-admit/tests/build.rs`: seven integration tests against production std, including native-input freshness and failures before assembly/after linking starts.
- `crates/tide-admit/tests/invocation.rs`: invalid build/profile arguments.
- `crates/tide-std/src/lib.rs`: parameterless builtin `#[test]` in production prelude; partial-runtime documentation.
- `conformance/cases/authority/root_executable.rs`: shared compile-time/production executable fixture.
- `conformance/README.md`: production/stub test equivalence and limits.
- `README.md`: build/test commands, profiles, outputs, caching and limits.
- `CODEX-REPORT.md`: scratch handoff; **never commit this file**.

## Checks

Offline, pinned `nightly-2026-08-09` (`771916f90`), with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` set to this worktree's `target`; conformance also uses its own local target. The main checkout's target was not used.

Candidate diff SHA-256: `b4386f1fd09cf295d44a8047d26172c1a65759ccd49a94a0540a66c76521413b` (tracked diff plus new-file diffs, excluding this scratch report).

- `cargo test --workspace`: **exit 0, 45 passed** (5 unit, 7 build, 13 driver, 14 invocation, 6 std entry).
- `conformance/run.sh`: **exit 0, 219 cases: 195 PASS, 24 AWAITS CHECKER, 0 FAIL**. The first run exited 1 solely because the new fixture listed runtime-only `SINK-1`; that ID was removed.
- `git diff --check`: exit 0.
- Pinned `cargo fmt --all`: exit 1, `cargo-fmt` is not installed; installed stable rustfmt formatted only touched Rust files.
- Fresh read-only Codex QA (`gpt-6.1-sol`, `xhigh`) found the native-input cache bug; its narrow re-check of the fix and strengthened tests is clean. This was not the formal governance round.

## Decisions for Opus

All recommendations below are implemented. Unqualified `invocation.rs` and `main.rs` mean the driver's `src/` files; `tests/build.rs` means its integration tests. Rust compiler references mean the installed pinned `rustc-src/rust/compiler/` sources. No design chapter was edited.

1. **Build boundary:** single checked compilation versus a second rustc invocation or Cargo. Recommend `--emit=link`, metadata default, only binaries/test harnesses: no second admission/snapshot gap or package hook path. Evidence: `invocation.rs:60`, `:166`; pinned `rustc_driver_impl/src/lib.rs:321` and `rustc_interface/src/passes.rs:1299` place error rejection before codegen. Alternatives require another input handoff and proof; rlib/object modes remain unexposed.

2. **Linker/host:** fixed system cc/ld versus bundled LLD or direct linker assembly. Recommend x86_64 Linux GNU only, `/usr/bin/cc`, GNU cc flavor, bundled linker disabled, `-B/usr/bin`. Evidence: `invocation.rs:223`; [GCC directory options](https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc/Directory-Options.html). The installed bundled-LLD wrapper failed with `/usr/bin/env: 'bash': No such file or directory` under the clean environment; system linking passed. Choosing LLD requires a clean-environment-compatible toolchain installation; broader hosts require their own fixed linker contract.

3. **Profiles:** debug only versus debug/release/custom. Recommend two fixed mappings: optimization 0/debug assertions on, or 3/off; overflow checks on in both, including metadata checks. Evidence: `invocation.rs:204`, `design/01-design.md:310`, `:779`, and [rustc options](https://doc.rust-lang.org/rustc/codegen-options/index.html). Different mappings change configuration identities and need runtime overflow proof again.

4. **Executable tests:** builtin harness versus Tide-specific test macros/runtime; caller execution versus automatic execution. Recommend builtin parameterless `#[test]`, built by `--test --emit=link`, executed separately by the trusted caller. Evidence: `tide-std/src/lib.rs:32`, `tests/build.rs:121`, shared fixture. A Tide runner requires simulation, isolation and structured-result work; no driver run flag is supplied.

5. **Caching:** one complete linked-build entry versus separate object/link caches. Recommend existing SHA-256 cache with normalized mode/profile/test arguments and cc/ld fingerprints; **no unsafe-granted link reuse** because native reads bypass snapshots. Evidence: `invocation.rs:751`, `:828`, `tests/build.rs:276`. Finer caches need stage identities; caching granted builds requires complete native-input ownership/dependency tracking.

6. **Outputs:** flat explicit output directory versus configuration/hash subdirectories. Recommend existing `--out-dir`, `<name>`/`<name>-test`, removing the requested old executable before checking. The shared `<name>.interface.json` belongs to the latest invocation; separate directories preserve configuration pairs. Evidence: `invocation.rs:247`, `:706`, `:865`; README examples. Different layout changes publication, cleanup, examples and consumers.

7. **Trusted demos:** operator review policy versus an acknowledgement flag or RUN-5 gate. Recommend explicit link opt-in plus operator review of source, grants, dependencies and native inputs, on a trusted host/toolchain. Evidence: `main.rs:25`, design RUN-2/RUN-5. An acknowledgement adds no enforcement; actual coverage gating needs the future reviewed-base/sandbox/snapshot machinery.

## Isolation limits recorded

No build/assembler/linker OS sandbox; granted assembly and native linking can read outside the loader. Host tools, startup objects and libraries remain trusted/immutable, not comprehensively fingerprinted. No concurrent filesystem-mutation protection. Caller execution has no driver-provided environment/descriptor/core-dump controls, Landlock/seccomp, simulated Root or snapshot/coverage gate. This does **not** satisfy RUN-5 or RUN-1's unreviewed-branch guarantee.

## Open problems / next steps

Opus should decide the seven choices, then run the formal parallel Opus/Codex governance round and subsequent confirmations before landing. Do not close the bead or commit this report yet.

Not checked: other hosts or RUN sandbox behavior. Risk: partial admission and unsandboxed native builds/execution require reviewed/trusted demos.

title: Define the Ferox comment and doc-comment syntax surface, attachment rules, and bootstrap support boundary
description: The tooling specs already assume file-level doc comments, declaration doc comments, and preserved comments in formatter recovery, but the language surface still lacks an explicit comment syntax decision. This task should define the concrete Ferox syntax for ordinary comments and doc comments, how they attach to modules and declarations, and what comment forms the bootstrap parser/formatter must support first.
design: Primary question: what exact comment and doc-comment forms should Ferox support, and how should they attach to source structure? Define: 1. whether Ferox uses line comments only, line plus block comments, and what doc-comment markers exist; 2. what counts as a file-level doc comment versus a declaration-attached doc comment; 3. how comments participate in the full-fidelity CST and formatter behavior; 4. what comment forms are intentionally out of scope for the first bootstrap parser if any.
acceptance_criteria: Done means this task clearly answers: the exact comment/doc-comment syntax forms; attachment and precedence rules; formatter and documentation implications; and bootstrap validation/logging expectations. Include concrete examples for file-level and declaration doc comments, rejected ambiguous alternatives, and explicit parser/formatter/doc-generation expectations.
notes: Decision: Ferox v1 uses a deliberately small comment surface: // for ordinary line comments, /// for declaration doc comments, and //// for file-level doc comments. Declaration docs attach to the next declaration; file-level docs attach to the file/module at the top of the file. Block comments and Rust-style inner-doc variants stay out of the v1 surface.

title: Run an autoresearch-style loop on checker speed once the checker exists
description:
Why: research/14-autoresearch.md finds Karpathy's autoresearch loop (frozen evaluator, one mutable file, keep-or-revert on one metric, a log of every attempt) does not fit Tide's design work but fits checker speed (D12 target: about 30 ms edit to diagnostics; D0 E4).

Start only after the v0 checker exists and has a test and conformance suite.

Scope:
- A frozen benchmark corpus and timing harness the loop cannot write to (the prepare.py role).
- One checker module or crate the agent may edit (the train.py role).
- Metric: median edit-to-diagnostics time on the corpus. Gate: the full test and conformance suite passes; a failing run is a discard.
- Keep-or-revert per attempt on one branch, an append-only results log (commit, time, status, description), and the simplicity rule: equal time with less code wins.
- An AP-EXCEPTION-001 exception the owner approves, bounded to that branch, since the loop runs without asking per step (AP-SCOPE-001, AP-PLAN-001, AP-GIT-001). Converge and the supervisor verdict still apply to the kept diff before it merges.

Out of scope: loops over design/reference.md or trial tasks (research/14 explains why), and the diagnostic-text loop, which gets its own bead if this one works.

Acceptance: the harness and corpus sit outside the agent's write set; one bounded run produces a results log and a kept diff whose speedup reproduces on a rerun of the harness; the kept diff passes the full suite.

Cheapest falsifier: if a bounded run keeps no change that reproduces, the loop is not worth its exception.

title: Define the new Ferox vision around safe change: low-entropy systems design, FP-shaped readability, fast feedback, and verification-ready tooling
description: Refine the Ferox vision into a sharper and more defensible thesis. The current direction under discussion is an ownership-based systems language for safe change: Rust-grade safe-code guarantees, lower semantic entropy than Rust, explicit performance behavior, FP-shaped readability, fast incremental feedback, and tooling designed for humans and agents to evolve large codebases without semantic drift.
design: Target shape: ADTs, exhaustive matching, expression-oriented code, immutable-by-default data flow, and a narrow pipe style inspired by the best parts of Gleam and Elixir, but without runtime magic or effect-heavy complexity. Keep ownership, mutation, async, and sharing explicit. Avoid syntax macros, trait/generic sprawl, and capability-heavy concurrency in the near term. Strengthen the tooling story around query-native incremental compilation, full-fidelity syntax trees, canonical formatting, structured diagnostics, normalized checked IR, and a first-party structural rule/autofix system. Treat verification as a later optional layer built around contracts, ghost/spec code, and proof-oriented tooling for critical modules rather than as a proof-first core language. Current version framing under discussion: v1 = Safe Core, v2 = Safe Change, v3 = Deep Assurance.
acceptance_criteria: A revised Ferox vision should clearly explain: 1. why Ferox exists if Rust already delivers strong safety; 2. what 'better for agents' means mechanically; 3. how FP influence improves readability without increasing entropy; 4. why fast feedback and incremental checking are core product requirements; 5. which high-leverage external ideas genuinely strengthen Ferox; 6. which ideas remain out of scope because they would widen the core too much; 7. how simple staged descriptions for v1, v2, and v3 follow from the thesis rather than feeling like unrelated feature buckets.
notes: The vision cleanup pass is now complete in principle: the accepted direction has been folded into the canonical docs, and the temporary draft vision files were removed to leave one primary vision set. .beads/.gitignore was also updated to ignore .br_history tracker artifacts produced by br.
close_reason: Vision rewrite completed in canonical docs; remaining work now lives in the narrower follow-on design beads.

true one passes 100 cases; each listed type generates. Toolchain tests prove it executes.

title: requires-guided generation, the vacuity floor, and sim_test parameters
description:
## Why

design/reference.md §10.2: #[requires] on a test or tested function filters and guides generation
(recognized shapes: scalar ranges, length bounds, index below length, is_sorted, contains, is_some,
x == c); a property test runs until 100 cases (or N for seeds = N) satisfy requires and fails as
`vacuous` below 1%, naming the conjunct that rejected most; a generated `seed: u64` with
Root::sim(seed), and `#[sim_test] fn t(sim: SimRoot, ...)` with extra generated parameters, give each
case its own simulator, and shrinking keeps the seed. Part of epic fx-m72 (E1-P12).

## Scope

The above on top of fx-m72.1's runner, fx-mhd's requires lowering and fx-nkv.6's #[sim_test] and
Root::sim. No new language semantics. Protocol §2 held-out rules apply.

## Acceptance

A vacuous property fails as vacuous and names the rejecting conjunct; a recognized shape is
generated directly (no vacuity failure for `i < xs.len()`); a #[sim_test] with an extra Vec<u16>
parameter shrinks it while keeping the seed. Toolchain tests prove each item executes.
close_reason: Landed 677a42b: requires-guided generation, vacuity floor, direct-callee discard, parameterized sim_test through the shared runner; Codex r1-r3, Opus r4-r5 approve; workspace 181, conformance 284/12/0. Open docs nit (meaning of 'evaluation' in the 300 s backstop) left as non-blocking.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Design decisions 2026-11-10 (coordinator Opus, from Fable research /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/tide-research-prop/report.md):
1. requires-guided generation: syntactic shape matching of top-level conjuncts against the reference's list (ranges, length bounds, i < xs.len(), is_sorted, contains, is_some, x == c, lo <= hi), ordering dependent parameters; the full requires is ALWAYS re-evaluated as a filter, so a misread shape costs only acceptance rate. Contradictory plans fall back to unconstrained generation. 'distinct' (04 but not the reference) is not implemented; report the 04/reference difference on fx-djp.
2. Vacuity floor: one stopping rule, generate until N cases are accepted or 100*N generated; not reached = vacuous, naming the conjunct with the most first rejections (short-circuit, source-order ties). Shrink candidates don't count. Passing tests print accepted/generated.
3. Callee rule: a 'requires violated' panic blamed on a call site in the test's own body discards the case; deeper is a failure; #[should_panic] never discards. Needs fx-mhd's structured violation payload.
4. sim_test with parameters lowers to the same runner; the simulator seed is the case seed, parameters draw from a stream derived from it, shrinking edits only parameters. A 'seed: u64' parameter on #[test] receives the case seed unshrunk (recorded as a reading of a provisional reference line).
5. Clause order: fx-mhd's requires macro moves itself below test/sim_test so attribute order can't silently disable guidance.

title: Generated contract tests and the E1 harness's test-runner stage
description:
## Why

design/reference.md §10.2 and design/04-contracts.md §2.4: `tide test` also tests every function
with an ensures on generated inputs that satisfy its requires, under the vacuity floor:
capabilities from a fresh Root::sim(seed), private-field types by random public constructor and
method calls that meet their requires, scalars over their full range, type parameters as i64 if it
meets the bounds, else String; ungeneratable functions are skipped as unchecked;
`#[allow(vacuous, reason = "..")]` reports a vacuous one as unchecked. E1's harness still fails
every Tide task's writer `./test` with a placeholder ('tide test runner unavailable',
trials/e1-checked/harness.py executable_tests). Part of epic fx-m72 (E1-P12).

## Scope

Generated contract tests in the toolchain, and replacing harness.py's R-stage placeholder with the
real runner so the Tide `./test` runs plain, property, simulation and generated contract tests as
protocol §4.1 states. Harness changes stay within protocol §2 and §6 (suites not frozen yet;
fx-ic2 freezes them). No new language semantics.

## Acceptance

A function whose ensures is violated on some generated input fails its generated test; a skipped
function is reported unchecked; #[allow(vacuous)] reports unchecked; harness.py no longer emits the
'tide test runner unavailable' record, and the writer ./test stage passes for every Tide reference
solution whose other prerequisites have closed (python3 trials/e1-checked/harness_test.py passes).
close_reason: Landed in 01712ea. Generated contract tests and the real E1 writer test runner. Reviews: Codex r1/r2/r4/r5, Opus r3/r4/r5, all clean at the end. Proof on 2a7ed4a: workspace 206 passed; conformance 288 PASS / 12 AWAITS / 0 FAIL; harness_test 22 OK; 19 references pass, 10 skipped for open owners; A4 fails with FX0401, a pre-existing reference/admission conflict recorded on fx-ic2.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Design decisions 2026-11-10 (coordinator Opus, from Fable research /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/tide-research-prop/report.md):
1. The driver owns generated contract tests (extends fx-m72.1's synthesis pass): from HIR, each fn with an ensures gets one #[test] in an injected child module with a reserved name, appended after the module's last user token so spans don't move.
2. Inputs: property-test generators guided by the fn's own requires under the same floor; type params i64 if bounds hold, else String, else skipped; private-field types via a public receiver-less constructor returning Self then 0-8 drawn public &mut self calls whose requires are checked first; capabilities from a fault-free Root::sim(seed); closure/dyn/handle params and unmet bounds -> unchecked.
3. Oracle: ensures violated or any other panic fails the test. Compile-time skips become #[ignore = "unchecked: <reason>"]; #[allow(vacuous, reason)] passes and prints 'unchecked (vacuous, allowed: ...)'. Laws are out of scope.
4. Harness: generated tests are excluded from the acceptance listing by filtering the reserved module segment when acceptance=True (protocol §7.2 puts them in the writer's ./test).

title: Define the Ferox explicit duplication model for copy-safe values, deep duplication, and generic duplication boundaries
description: The ownership spec now makes copy-safe values explicit, but the exact explicit-duplication surface is still intentionally open. This task should define how Ferox handles deliberate deep duplication for non-copy values, what generic constraints or library hooks are allowed, and how duplication remains visible without letting copy/clone semantics become muddy or trait-heavy.
design: Primary question: how should Ferox express explicit duplication for non-copy values while keeping copy-safe behavior simple and ownership reasoning local? Define: 1. whether duplication is a built-in operation, library function, trait-backed convention, or staged combination; 2. how generic code states duplication requirements; 3. what types may never be duplicated or only duplicated through domain-specific APIs; 4. how diagnostics and tooling should explain copy-safe versus explicit-duplication boundaries.
acceptance_criteria: Done means this task clearly answers: what syntax or API shape Ferox uses for explicit duplication; how generic duplication boundaries work; how duplication differs from implicit copy; and what stays out of scope. Include at least one recommended example, one rejected alternative, validation expectations for copy-safe versus explicit-duplication cases, and logging expectations for duplication eligibility diagnostics.
close_reason: Superseded: the owner discarded the first Ferox design (archived in archive/v0-design/) for the first-principles redesign in fx-agent-first-redesign-tf4; this work no longer applies.

title: Executable contract clauses
description:
## Why

E1's gate run (fx-ic2) needs this surface to execute on the checked toolchain:
`trials/e1-checked/protocol.md` §10.1 lists it as E1-P11, and no existing bead owns it.

## Evidence

- `trials/e1-checked/protocol.md (§10.1 row E1-P11, §10.2)`
- `design/reference.md §10.1; design/04-contracts.md`

## Scope

#[requires], #[ensures], #[invariants], invariant!, old, result, ==>, and bounded forall/exists lowered by the production toolchain macros, checked in debug and test builds and erased in release, with the violation panic text 10.1 gives. Production std under crates/, built and admitted through tide-admit; no new
language semantics.

## Acceptance

A violated clause panics with requires/ensures/invariant violated and the clause text; checked and sampled clauses run as 10.1 states; release builds erase them. Toolchain tests prove each item executes, not only type-checks.
Std API changes must also satisfy fx-nkv acceptance on production/conformance equivalence; the production library owns runtime behavior.

Interface for fx-m72.2: requires blame on the direct call site; ensures marker = a call to __contract::ensures (runtime) or __contract::const_ensures_marker (const) in the fn's own HIR body. One code shape in every profile; only execution is gated by constants (04 §2.6 type-checks release clauses).
2. old(e) lowers to (e).clone() method syntax (Copy copies, &T snapshots referent, neither -> E0599), evaluated after all requires checks in clause order; nested old and old naming result or a binder rejected.
3. Entry values of params named in ensures outside old: autoref-dispatch std helper (Copy copy, Clone clone, else read in place); fallback to read-in-place plus syntactic copies if fragile, recorded here.
4. result: let result = call; ensures closures capture &result; explicit -> R unless impl Trait; call-site hygiene; FX0805 kept.
5. Quantifiers: std helpers __contract::forall/exists(_in) that short-circuit and count steps; signed binder needs lo <= i; only CLAUSE-1's guard shapes (x <= hi rejected); ==> right-assoc lowest precedence.
6. invariant!: for over a..b reads Range.start as the next index (exit = max(a,b)); other for loops use rustc's match desugaring (keeps temporaries); while let -> loop { check; match }; loop gets head checks only; debug non-test checks a..b at entry/exit only; a..=b treated as 'any other iterator'.
7. Violations: one #[track_caller] std helper per kind evaluating the clause under catch_unwind; false or panic -> String payload 'requires violated: <clause source text>' + function + blamed span (+ '(clause panicked: ..)'); requires blames the caller via #[track_caller]; ensures/invariant embed the clause's own span. A structured record (kind, clause index, conjunct, function) goes to a thread-local readable through a hidden std accessor before the panic.
8. Classes: checked = cfg!(debug_assertions); sampled = cfg!(debug_assertions) && cfg!(test) (dependencies' sampled clauses listed unchecked); syntax-based classification, unclassifiable runs as checked; budget = one step per binder value counted in std with a fixed default recorded in 04; over-budget clauses recorded as unchecked in std for runners to print. Sampled invariant schedule per 04 §2.4. Confirm admission of generated cfg!, else const-item fallback.
9. Markers for admission: clause bodies are closure literals passed to ::std::__contract::* items, which the driver recognizes by definition (FX0808 purity, placement FX0802 are fx-u65.6's).
10. Interface for fx-m72.2/.3 (supersedes item 2 of the earlier interface comment): no separate predicate functions; each requires attribute and top-level conjunct is its own helper call, and the thread-local record lets a runner classify a caught panic as 'requires rejected' and name the conjunct. Attribute order: a contract macro that finds test or sim_test among the remaining attributes re-emits the item with that test attribute outermost, so the test macro sees the clauses.
11. The conformance stub switches from the spike macros to tide-macros in this bead, updating pinned error codes in the same change.

title: Decide: run /correct from the session runner
description:
## Decision

Should the session runner (fx-3md) also run Starcompass's `correct` skill on
a schedule, so repeated owner corrections turn into decision beads without the
owner asking?

Recommendation: adopt, once fx-3md exists. Run `/correct` in a fresh headless
session when the runner stops with no work left, and otherwise at most once
every 10 sessions. Tide's "Decisions" rule makes this an agent decision.
Record it here, then do the work below or close this as rejected.

Owner suggestion, 2026-10-21: the owner asked why agents do not run `correct`
on their own, and asked for this as a decision.

## Why

`correct` (Starcompass `skills/correct`, linked into `~/.claude/skills` by
`skills/install.sh`) reads the owner's typed and queued messages from this
project's Claude Code sessions. It groups corrections that repeat across
sessions and files one bead per class, proposing the strongest enforcement:
structure, then checks, then trials, then wording. Skills run only when invoked
or matched, and nothing invokes this one. So the owner's corrections stay
buried in transcripts unless the owner remembers to type `/correct`.

## Evidence

- Starcompass `ap-1bu` (closed 2026-10-21): the skill, its converge rounds,
  and an isolated trial that correctly found real corrections and filed
  nothing below the two-session threshold.
- `~/.claude/projects/-home-lucca-pjs-lab-tide/` held 23 sessions with 116
  owner messages on 2026-10-21. That is enough history for real classes.

## Scope

In scope:
- The fx-3md runner: one more trigger that starts `/correct` in its own
  session, plus a run-log line for it.

Out of scope:
- The `correct` skill itself, which Starcompass owns. Report changes it needs
  there.
- Acting on the beads it files. They are decisions for later sessions.

## Acceptance

- The runner starts a `/correct` session when it stops with no work left, and
  at most once every 10 sessions otherwise.
- Each `/correct` run leaves one log line: time, the beads it filed or
  "none", and its cost.
- Two runs in a row over unchanged history file no duplicate beads.

title: Scope TASK-3: by-value arguments, Bend call cancellation, uninterruptible file I/O
description:
## Why

TASK-3 makes two claims that real operations do not meet. First, "checkpoints that consume a value
return it inside the error": read literally, that covers arguments passed by value to a checkpoint,
such as `Fs::write(p, vec)` and `write_synced` (`impl AsRef<[u8]>`), path arguments,
`Net::connect(addr)`, and Bend kernel calls that consume `board` (03 §10). Their errors have no room
for the value, and `BendFault` has no cancellation variant although 03 §1.1 says every capability
error type has one. Second, "an in-flight kernel operation is cancelled before the error returns":
Linux regular-file I/O and `fsync` (on NFS, for example) sleep uninterruptibly, so `write` and
`sync` can overrun a deadline, even a shielded scope's, just as `File::close` can, while TASK-5
names only `close`. Found by rounds 73 and 74 while reviewing fx-nyy; both predate it.

## Evidence

- `design/03-authority-concurrency.md` §1.1 intro (cancellation variants), TASK-3, TASK-5, §10
  (Bend calls are checkpoints).
- `design/reference.md` 6.3 (`Fs` signatures), 7.2.
- `reviews/round73-consistency.md` (out-of-scope findings); `reviews/round74-consistency.md`
  (out-of-scope finding, with suggested TASK-3 and TASK-5 wording).

## Scope

In scope: say which by-value arguments TASK-3's return rule covers (for example, only values the
operation delivers or keeps, such as `send` and `write_owned`, not arguments it only reads); give
Bend calls a cancellation story consistent with §1.1; state in TASK-3 and TASK-5 which kernel
operations cannot be cancelled in flight and what that does to deadlines. State it in 03 and,
within D14's budget, the reference pair.

Out of scope: `File::close` (fx-nyy decided it).

## Acceptance

- 03 decides each point with reasoning; the reference pair does not contradict it.
- The core stays under D14's budget (it is at 24,999 of 25,000; recount with
  `scripts/count-tokens.sh`, trimming elsewhere if needed).
- A review round in `reviews/` finds no contradiction.

## Notes

Docs-only: review rounds, not converge.
close_reason: Decided in 03 TASK-3, TASK-5, §1.1 Receivers note, §9.3, §10; core 7.2 and D8 wording. Reviews: rounds 94-97 (Opus), 98 (Codex, approve). Follow-ups: fx-e3t.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Decision (03 TASK-3, TASK-5, §1.1 Receivers note, §10 Accel and Failures; core 7.2 and 01 D8 wording):
1. TASK-3's return rule covers values a checkpoint hands over: channel payloads and owned buffers (send, read_owned, write_owned). Arguments it only reads (impl AsRef data, paths, addresses, Bend arguments copied to the server) are dropped with the call; callers that need them pass a reference or a clone. Reason: returning every argument would need a generic error type per operation, and AsRef already lets callers keep ownership. Core 7.2 and D8 say 'hand a value over' instead of 'consume a value'.
2. BendFault gains Cancelled (is_cancelled() true), satisfying §1.1. Process mode abandons the request and restarts the server; in-process mode cannot stop a running kernel, which finishes first like a foreign call.
3. Kernel calls the kernel cannot cancel once running (regular-file reads, writes, fsync) run to the end and return their own result; the task observes cancellation at its next checkpoint, so a finished write reports success. Rejected: reporting Cancelled after the effect happened (hides a completed write). Multi-call operations (fs.write, remove_dir_all) check between calls and can stop partway. TASK-5 lists a running regular-file kernel call; with close, it can block on NFS inside a shielded scope with a deadline.
Core at 24,996 of 25,000.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Revision after round 94 (B1, B2, N1-N4, N6): (1) TASK-3/TASK-5 name the class: file-system calls on regular files and directories (reads, writes, fsync, opens, renames, removals, metadata queries, directory reads) cannot be cancelled once running and return their own result; 'system call' replaces 'kernel call' (Bend's kernel calls differ). (2) A cancellable call that completes before the cancel takes effect returns its own result; a call with no effect (name lookup) may be abandoned. (3) Multi-call operations check before each call they start except a final close; a cancelled fs.write can leave its target truncated. (4) The simulator follows the same rules; simulated Bend cancellation follows the declared mode. (5) In-process Bend: a running kernel finishes and returns its own result, cancellation observed at the next checkpoint; a call still waiting for the serialized runtime returns BendFault::Cancelled. Not applied: N6's 'Unlike send' marker (nit).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Revision after round 95 (B1, N1-N3, N5): a library call the kernel cannot cancel and that has no effect, such as a name lookup, is abandoned and returns the cancellation error (always, not 'may'); this is distinct from system calls, so file reads are never abandoned. The run-to-end rule covers any system call the kernel cannot cancel, file-system calls being the main case. Socket and pipe waits are cancellable; a cancelled socket or pipe write may have reached the peer. Multi-call operations check before each call except a close. §9.3: cancellation cuts a modeled latency short only where TASK-3 lets it; simulated stdin behaves as a pipe. Bend process mode returns Cancelled unless the reply already arrived; in-process Bend is a foreign call. Not applied: N4 (companion note on soft cleanup deadlines; pre-existing core 7.2 gap).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Revision after round 96 (B1, N1, N2, N4): the abandonment rule names its member: 'A name lookup, a library call that cannot be cancelled and has no effect, is abandoned instead and returns the cancellation error; it runs on, on its own copy of the name, and its result is discarded. A foreign call, such as an in-process Bend kernel, is not abandoned (TASK-5, §10).' TASK-5 lists 'a running system call the kernel cannot cancel (TASK-3)', matching TASK-3. TASK-3 split into three paragraphs; wording fixes. Not applied: N3 (is_terminal under the simulator; optional). Pre-existing finding to file: cancelled output()/status() can orphan a child.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Codex round 98 approved. Not applied: its N1 (FUSE can honor interrupts, so file-system run-to-end is Tide's policy rather than a kernel limit on every file system); the behavior stands as written, and it is a wording precision for a later pass. Follow-ups filed as fx-e3t.

title: Define the Ferox safe-change tooling contract as a concrete machine-facing product surface
description: Synthesize the Ferox tooling contract from the now-separated read-side and mutation-side machine interfaces. This bead should consolidate those decisions into one coherent official safe-change tooling contract that compiler architecture and later tooling work can rely on.
design:
Primary question: Given the read-side and mutation-side machine contracts, what is the final integrated Ferox safe-change tooling contract?

This synthesis task should:
1. Reconcile machine-readable outputs with machine-driven mutation surfaces.
2. Define the official contract boundary, stability story, and phase-by-phase rollout.
3. Produce the canonical tooling contract that architecture and bootstrap tasks can reference without ambiguity.
4. Carry forward compatibility, observability, and validation requirements in one place.

title: Define the Ferox machine-readable read contract for diagnostics, symbols, metadata, and determinism
description: Ferox's safe-change tooling story depends first on stable machine-readable outputs that tools can consume reliably. This task defines the read-side contract: diagnostics, spans, symbol identity, symbol graphs, project/package metadata, formatter output expectations, and determinism guarantees.

Primary question: What official machine-readable outputs should Ferox tools be able to consume reliably from day one and beyond?

Define:
1. Diagnostic structure, spans, codes, related information, and suggested-fix shape.
2. Stable symbol identity, symbol graph, and package/project metadata outputs.
3. Expectations for deterministic formatting/build-related outputs where they are part of the toolchain contract.
4. Stability and versioning expectations for these read-side outputs.

This task should define the read contract that later compiler services and automation can depend on.
