title: Case-study round: crypto/blockchain Rust crates (std-concurrency and deterministic-logic crates; retrospective + forward hunt + admission observations)
description:
## Why
Relayed owner decision (Lucca via tide-desk, 2026-11-18; recorded as relayed by tide-lead). He shared @gakonst's post (Paradigm CTO; Reth, Foundry), which values automated testing and agents writing properties and models. Lucca: "we can do a crypto pass / since these guys like correctness". His "until we found, our search continues" covers it. The round has three arms on crypto and blockchain Rust code: past concurrency fixes, a forward property hunt, and admission observations.

## Frozen search criteria (pre-registered by tide-lead, 2026-11-18, before any repository is examined)
The criteria are frozen here. A builder adds operational detail in a protocol file. The protocol and the pool files are COMMITTED on the bead branch and OpenTimestamps-stamped, and tide-lead records their SHA-256s and upgrades the proofs, all before "go". The protocol may narrow these criteria; it may never widen them or change a caught rule. The GitHub rule in standing decisions applies: repository search sliced by stars, never commit search, throttled.

**Repositories.** GitHub repository search, `language:Rust stars:>=1000 archived:false fork:false topic:<t>`, for each topic t in: blockchain, ethereum, cryptocurrency, web3, solana, bitcoin, zk, zero-knowledge, evm, defi, smart-contracts, cryptography. Each query is sliced by stars to stay under the 1,000-result cap. Record every query, its time and its response SHA-256. Use the union of distinct repositories. Each repository's default-branch HEAD is pinned by a read-only clone (`--filter=blob:none`; check out only what the scan needs).

**Crate-level scan.** Every Cargo package in each repository's workspace (non-test library or binary source; exclude tests/, benches/, examples/, `#[cfg(test)]`) is classified, mechanically, by a committed script:
- **Class C (std concurrency):** fx-zu4f.10's filter at crate level. It uses std thread, mpsc, Mutex, RwLock or atomics; it has no Condvar, select!, async/.await, Waker or `unsafe impl Send/Sync`; and it has no normal dependency on tokio, futures, async-std, crossbeam*, parking_lot*, rayon*, flume or loom.
- **Class P (deterministic logic):** no async/.await; none of those dependencies; no use of std::net, std::process, std::fs or std::thread; no `unsafe` block or fn; between 200 and 5,000 lines of non-test source; and at least one `#[test]` of its own. This holds the state machines, orderings, nonce and fee logic, and encodings that a seeded property test fits.
- Everything else is excluded, with its first reason.

**Pool.** Kept crates are ordered by repository stars, descending, then repository full name, then crate name. At most 3 crates per repository (the first 3 in that order), for spread. Pool = the first 30. If fewer are kept, the pool is all of them.

**Arm B (retrospective), class C crates only.** Candidates are the commits that touch the crate's own directory, from the frozen clone, whose full message matches, case-insensitively: `\b(race|races|racy|racing|deadlock|deadlocks|deadlocked|dead-lock|hang|hangs|hanging|hung|livelock|lost wakeup|data race|stuck|freeze|freezes|frozen|starvation|starve|starved)\b`. The word boundaries are deliberate: fx-zu4f.10's unbounded regex matched 'change' and 'trace' and gave 5,076 rows. E1-E5, the faithful model, the property and the caught rule are exactly fx-zu4f.10's.

**Arm A (forward hunt), the first 10 pool crates.** As fx-zu4f.10's arm A:
- Port the crate's core (concurrent core for class C, its state machine or logic for class P) faithfully into Tide v0, within 400 lines, with every model gap recorded.
- Properties only from the crate's docs, tests and asserted or documented invariants, quoted, and written BEFORE any run.
- 1,000 seeds, using #[sim_test] for class C and a seeded property test for class P.
- The new-bug caught rule needs: a failing seed; two byte-identical replays; a control model that passes all 1,000; AND reproduction on the real crate at its pinned commit (a real-thread stress test or existing loom for C; the crate's own test harness for P), built offline through heavy.sh in TARGET.

**Admission observations (descriptive, never a catch).** For every pool crate, and every class-excluded binary or CLI crate in a pool repository, a committed script counts with file:line the ambient std::env, std::fs, std::net and std::process uses and detached spawns. It flags those within the same function as key, seed, mnemonic, secret or private-key handling (mechanical, by identifier match; state the rule). Reported separately.

**Safety.** Never contact a live network, mainnet or testnet; everything is local or simulated. No key material beyond published test vectors. Never run code that could sign or broadcast.

**Disclosure.** The policy on fx-zu4f.10 and fx-qlek.7 applies, with these additions:
- crypto finds are classified dangerous by default when funds, consensus or keys could be affected;
- each project's security program (Immunefi, HackerOne, SECURITY.md) is recorded with its URL and the date read, and its rules bind the report draft;
- agents draft into ~/.cache/eon-agents/tide-lead/fx-zu4f.12-private/ and Lucca sends;
- a private find counts for the RC only once it is fixed and disclosed.

**Never:** widen the pool, the criteria or a caught rule; build or run upstream code except arm A's reproduction step; post upstream; judge the authors.

## Acceptance
- Before "go": protocol, pool files and .ots proofs committed on branch fx-zu4f.12; SHA-256s recorded here; proofs upgraded.
- The record lists every pool crate and arm-B candidate with its first failure and reason, counts by arm, negatives first, and the admission observations separately.
- A catch becomes a case study under the privacy and disclosure rules.
- GOVERNANCE Merge Rule. The branch lands by merge.
- Scheduling: after fx-zu4f.10 and fx-zu4f.11, under the agent cap.

title: Case-study round: landed-capability re-screen (rows of fx-zu4f.5-.11 that failed only for a since-landed Proc/Net capability)
description:
## Why
Desk decision (tide-desk, 2026-11-18, within Lucca's relayed "until we found, our search continues"; recorded by tide-lead on fx-zu4f.10). fx-zu4f.10's B09.003, a bindgen child-pipe deadlock, failed E4 only because v0 had no subprocess capability, and Proc::command has since landed (fx-ayh2.1, e0b0d62). This round re-screens EVERY such row against current main. It is the race-side twin of fx-zu4f.8, which re-screens the malware advisories under the new capabilities. Filing it was authorized as one more fx-zu4f round, once fx-zu4f.10's arm B completed (done 2026-11-18 21:51Z).

## Frozen criteria (tide-lead, 2026-11-18, before the pool is built)
- **Pool, mechanical:** every row in the COMMITTED records of fx-zu4f.5 through fx-zu4f.11 (both arms) whose ONLY first-failure reason is a capability Tide v0 lacked at that round's registered revision and which has since LANDED on main (today: subprocess, by Proc::command; network, by Net::get once fx-ff13 lands). A row with any other failing reason (async, external crates, a core over 400 lines, an OS trigger, memory unsafety, unresolved dispatch) is NOT in the pool. Rows are taken from committed records only, never from private notes. Known members so far: fx-zu4f.10 B09.003 (arm B) and arm-A rank 9, bindgen (both cap:proc).
- **Disclosure:** the pool is defined AFTER those rows were seen. The trigger is a capability landing, not the bug. The record states this first.
- **Freeze and stamp:** the pool file and protocol are committed on branch fx-zu4f.13 and OpenTimestamps-stamped, with SHA-256s recorded here and proofs upgraded, before "go".
- **Rules:** E1-E5, the faithful model, the property and the caught rule are exactly those of the source row's round, judged against current main's v0, with the capability's landing commit named. Nothing else is relaxed.
- **Privacy and disclosure:** as on fx-zu4f.10 and fx-qlek.7.

## Acceptance
- Protocol and pool committed and OTS-stamped before go, with SHA-256s recorded here and proofs upgraded.
- The record lists every pool row with its outcome, negatives first, and states the post-hoc pool.
- GOVERNANCE Merge Rule; the branch lands by merge.
- Scheduling: after fx-ff13 lands (so a network-only row, if any, is judged against Net too), under the agent cap.

title: Case-study round: post-quantum crypto Rust crates (randomness as a capability; KAT-seeded properties; admission observations)
description:
## Why
Relayed owner decision (Lucca via tide-desk, 2026-11-18; recorded as relayed by tide-lead). Lucca: "We can also investigate quantum algorithms". tide-desk offered two angles, (a) post-quantum crypto libraries as a search pool and (b) quantum programming as a future Tide domain. Lucca: "These two angles". This bead is (a). It is covered by "until we found, our search continues": rounds are filed one at a time, and this one comes after fx-zu4f.12.

## Frozen search criteria (pre-registered by tide-lead, 2026-11-18, before any repository is examined)
The protocol may narrow these criteria, never widen them or change a caught rule. The GitHub rule and the owner-affiliation exclusion in standing decisions apply.

**Repositories.** Recorded GitHub repository search (sliced by stars, never commit search, throttled) plus recorded crates.io search, for Rust code implementing a NIST post-quantum algorithm or a post-quantum protocol:
- algorithms: ML-KEM/Kyber, ML-DSA/Dilithium, SLH-DSA/SPHINCS+, FN-DSA/Falcon, HQC, Classic McEliece;
- protocols: e.g. rosenpass, post-quantum TLS or Noise.
The query list, times and response SHA-256s are recorded. A repository needs at least 1,000 stars at the repo level; a crate in an org repository such as RustCrypto's counts by that repository's stars. Repositories owned by Yazelix or luccahuguet are excluded up front. Default-branch HEADs are pinned by read-only clones.

**Crate-level classes:** exactly fx-zu4f.12's class C (std-only concurrency) and class P (deterministic logic), applied by a committed script; everything else is excluded with its first reason. **Pool ordering and caps:** as fx-zu4f.12 (stars descending, at most 3 crates per repository, first 30).

**Tide's angle, stated in the protocol:** RANDOMNESS AS A CAPABILITY. Keygen, encapsulation and signing that reach ambient OS randomness; RNG reuse; determinism bugs that a seeded replay exposes.
- Admission observations (descriptive, never a catch): with file:line, count ambient randomness sources (getrandom, OsRng, thread_rng, rand::random, /dev/urandom) and where they enter keygen, encapsulation or signing; plus std::env, fs, net and process uses, as in fx-zu4f.12.
- Forward hunt (first 10 pool crates): seeded property tests with the crate's own KATs (known-answer tests) as oracles, plus properties quoted from its docs and tests and written before any run. The caught rule is fx-zu4f.12's, including reproduction on the real crate at its pinned commit.
- Arm B (class C crates only): fx-zu4f.12's word-bounded regex and E1-E5.

**Out of class, stated plainly in the protocol and the record:** constant-time and side-channel bugs (for example KyberSlash), timing leaks, and fault attacks. Tide's model does not see them.

**Expected yield is low**, and the record says so up front.

**Safety:** no live keys, only published test vectors; never contact a network; never run code that could sign or broadcast anything real.

**Disclosure:** the fx-zu4f.10, fx-qlek.7 and fx-zu4f.12 rules apply. Crypto finds are dangerous by default. Each project's security policy is recorded with its URL and the date read, and binds the draft. Drafts go to ~/.cache/eon-agents/tide-lead/fx-zu4f.14-private/; Lucca sends. A private find counts for the RC only once it is fixed and disclosed.

## Acceptance
- Before "go": protocol, pool files and .ots proofs committed on branch fx-zu4f.14, SHA-256s recorded here, proofs upgraded.
- The record lists every pool crate and candidate with its first failure, negatives first; admission observations separately; the out-of-class limits and the low expected yield stated first.
- GOVERNANCE Merge Rule; the branch lands by merge.
- Scheduling: after fx-zu4f.12, under the agent cap.

title: Case study: an external bug that Tide's admission rejects (pre-registered search)
description:
## Why
The case studies so far are fx-zu4f.2 (Eon), fx-zu4f.3 (hyper) and fx-zu4f.4 (Eon). Admission catches none of their bugs; simulation and tests do. The owner, 2026-11-18, relayed by tide-desk: "But we need to find one of these / And it has to be external. Not eon." This bead is an exception to the no-new-beads rule, authorized for exactly this bead, and it blocks the alpha RC (fx-qlek.7). Parent: fx-zu4f.

## Frozen search criteria (pre-registered by tide-lead, 2026-11-18, before any candidate is examined)
The criteria are frozen here, before any search. A builder may add operational detail in a protocol file, but must commit it and have tide-lead record its SHA-256 on this bead before examining any candidate. That file may narrow the criteria; it may never widen them or change the caught rule.

**Source pools.** Examine every candidate each pool yields, and record each one.
- **P1, malicious crates:** every RustSec advisory (github.com/rustsec/advisory-db, at a commit recorded at search time) that reports a crates.io crate as malicious, published up to 2026-11-18. Among the candidates tide-desk named to check: rustdecimal (2022), faster_log and async_println (2025).
- **P2, accidental ambient effects:** GitHub issues and pull requests in Rust repositories with at least 1,000 stars. Run each of these queries once on the search date and take the first 10 results each, by GitHub's default sort, recording the date and the result list:
  - "env::var" bug;
  - "SystemTime::now" flaky;
  - "hardcoded path";
  - "thread" "outlives";
  - "global state" bug;
  - "std::process::Command" unexpected.

  Count only closed issues, or merged PRs, that describe a real bug with a fix. Mark every other result as not a candidate, with the reason.

**Bug classes** (anything else is out of class):
- ambient fs, env, net, process or clock use;
- a detached spawn;
- global mutable state;
- `unsafe` without a grant.

**Caught rule.**

title: Case study: an external concurrency bug found by a seeded sim_test and replayed (pre-registered search)
description:
## Why
The case studies so far (fx-zu4f.2 and .4, on Eon) show simulation and replay catching real races, but only in Eon. We never searched outside Eon for that kind of bug. Owner, 2026-11-18, relayed by tide-desk: "then do it!". This bead is an exception to the no-new-beads rule, authorized for exactly this bead. It blocks the alpha RC (fx-qlek.7). Parent: fx-zu4f. Discipline as in fx-zu4f.5: pre-registered criteria, a registered protocol, every candidate recorded, never stretched.

## Frozen search criteria (pre-registered by tide-lead, 2026-11-18, before any candidate is examined)
The criteria are frozen here, before any search. A builder may add operational detail in a protocol file, but must commit it and have tide-lead record its SHA-256 on this bead before examining any candidate. That file may narrow the criteria; it may never widen them or change the caught rule.

**Pool.** Use the GitHub REST search/issues endpoint, read-only. Run each query below exactly once on the search date, with `language:Rust is:issue is:closed` appended, `per_page=20`, `page=1`, and GitHub's default sort. Take the first N = 20 results of each and record the date, the request, `total_count` and the ordered list.
1. `"race condition" in:title`
2. `flaky in:title`
3. `intermittent in:title`
4. `deadlock in:title`
5. `"data race" in:title`
6. `"lost update"`
7. `org:tokio-rs race`
8. `"std::thread" race`

Apply these after the cap, with no refill:
- the repository has at least 1,000 stars, and its primary language is Rust;
- it is not Eon or Tide (or a fork of either).
Results failing either check are recorded as not candidates. Duplicate URLs across queries are assessed once and cross-linked.

**Eligibility** (all must hold; record each failure's reason):
- E1: a public fix, a merged PR or commit linked from the issue or its timeline;
- E2: the issue states the reported symptom, the observed wrong behavior;
- E3: the bug is concurrency-shaped: a race, lost update, ordering fault, deadlock, or timing-dependent flake;
- E4: the affected code path is small enough to model faithfully in Tide v0, with no network, no subprocess and no external crates. Tide's simulated Fs, Clock, tasks, channels and Shared are allowed.

**Faithful model.**
- Model only the affected code path: keep its structure, its shared state and its interleaving points (awaits, locks, channel operations, spawns). Change nothing beyond what Tide v0's syntax and std require.
- Record every model gap, as the Eon studies did.
- The fixed model applies the fix commit's change and nothing else.
- The buggy model contains no bug the source lacks.
- Not portable: a candidate whose path needs more than this is "unportable", with the reason.

**Property.** It comes from the issue's own reported expected behavior. Write it in the search record, with a quote or link, before any test of that candidate runs. It is never adjusted after a run.

**Caught rule** (seed budget frozen at 1,000 seeds, seeds 0..999, `#[sim_test(seeds = 1000)]` or its equivalent):
- the buggy model fails the property on at least one seed in the budget;
- replaying a failing seed twice through the driver's recording (`tide-admit --tide-run-test … --seed N`, then `--replay`) reproduces byte-identical traces;
- the fixed model passes all 1,000 seeds.

A candidate that fails any of the three is "not caught", with the reason. Detection by admission alone does not count here.

## Scope
- Under `examples/case-studies/<name>/`, following eon-discovery-race and the fx-rpsb.1 runner conventions: the buggy model, with the failure declared as its expected outcome; the fixed model, passing; and a write-up. The write-up cites the issue, the fix commit and the license, gives the property with its source quote, the model and its gaps, and the seed and replay evidence. Negatives come first: what Tide does not do (it found nothing unaided; the property was supplied; the bug was already fixed upstream), and what Rust needs for the same test (loom, Shuttle, tokio's test utilities, and so on).
- A search record listing every result with its query, its eligibility outcome and reason, and, for each eligible candidate, caught, not caught or unportable, with the reason. It goes in research/ or the case study's directory.
- Report the counts: screened, eligible, caught, not caught, unportable. Present the catch as a demonstration, never as a rate.
- If several are caught, pick the shortest faithful model, breaking ties by the clearest issue and fix evidence; list the others in the record.
- If none qualifies, land the record as a documented negative and write no case study. Never stretch a candidate.

Out of scope: changes to the driver, std, runner, reference or companion; Eon and Tide bugs; posting anything upstream (outreach follows fx-zu4f's rule).

## Acceptance
- The frozen criteria above are followed, and the record lists every result with counts.
- If one is caught: `cargo test --workspace` through heavy.sh passes on the landed tree, with the buggy model's failure and the fixed model's pass as declared outcomes, and the record shows the byte-identical replay.
- If none is caught: the record lands as a documented negative, and fx-qlek.7 is told.
- GOVERNANCE.md's Merge Rule: a Codex pass, then an Opus converge round that reports instead of fixing. If Codex's cyber filter trips, an Opus stand-in reviews and the refusal is recorded.

title: Case study: an external std-level concurrency bug found by a seeded sim_test and replayed (second pre-registered round)
description:
## Why
fx-zu4f.6 searched broad GitHub queries and found no eligible external race: 126 of 158 unique results were from repositories under 1,000 stars, and 15 of the 32 screened failed E4 because their code path crosses an external crate. Owner, 2026-11-18, relayed by tide-desk, answering "1 = one more pre-registered round on a std-level concurrency pool (recommended), 2 = top-30 repositories, 3 = stop": "1". The reason for this pool: its code paths are std-level, so the external-crate cut should shrink. Discipline as in fx-zu4f.5 and .6: pre-registered criteria, a registered protocol, every result recorded, never stretched.

## Frozen search criteria (pre-registered by tide-lead, 2026-11-18, before any candidate is examined)
The criteria are frozen here, before any search. A builder may add operational detail in a protocol file, but must commit it and have tide-lead record its SHA-256 on this bead before examining any candidate. That file may narrow the criteria; it may never widen them or change the caught rule.

Take the first N = 10 results of each and record the date, the request, `total_count` and the ordered list.

Repositories (7):
- R1 `repo:rust-lang/rust label:T-libs`
- R2 `repo:crossbeam-rs/crossbeam`
- R3 `repo:Amanieu/parking_lot`
- R4 `repo:xacrimon/dashmap`
- R5 `repo:zesterer/flume`
- R6 `repo:matklad/once_cell`
- R7 `repo:rayon-rs/rayon`

Terms (8): T1 `race`, T2 `deadlock`, T3 `"lost wakeup"`, T4 `"lost update"`, T5 `"data race"`, T6 `spurious`, T7 `hang`, T8 `intermittent`.

That makes 56 queries, each run once. Duplicate URLs across queries are assessed once and cross-linked. If a repository has moved, use the address GitHub's search resolves and record it; never substitute a different project.

**Scope filter** (applied before eligibility, recorded as "not a candidate" with the reason):
- R1: the issue concerns std's sync or thread modules: mpsc and channels, Once and OnceLock, LazyLock, Mutex, RwLock, Condvar, Barrier, thread::scope, park and unpark, or atomics-based std types. Compiler, codegen, MIR, LLVM, platform-ABI and toolchain bugs are excluded.
- R2: crossbeam's channel, deque, epoch, queue or utils crates.
- R7: rayon-core only (the scheduler, the registry, job and latch code), not rayon's parallel-iterator adaptors.

**Eligibility** (all must hold; record each failure's reason):
- E1: a public fix, a merged PR or commit linked from the issue or its timeline;
- E2: the issue states the reported symptom, the observed wrong behavior;
- E3: the bug is concurrency-shaped: a race, lost update, lost wakeup, ordering fault, deadlock or hang, or a timing-dependent flake;
- E4: the affected code path is small enough to model faithfully in Tide v0, with no network, no subprocess and no external crates. Tide's simulated Fs, Clock, tasks, channels and Shared are allowed, plus whatever Tide v0 std offers for the operations the path uses;
- E5: the bug does not depend on what Tide's simulator cannot explore. It must not need memory orderings weaker than the simulator's (a bug that appears only under Relaxed, Acquire or Release reordering is not eligible), real OS scheduling or preemption semantics beyond task interleavings at the simulator's scheduling points, or hardware or platform behavior. State each candidate's model gaps, including any atomic operation modeled as an interleaving point under sequential consistency.

**Faithful model.**
- Model only the affected code path: keep its structure, its shared state and its interleaving points (awaits, locks, channel operations, spawns). Change nothing beyond what Tide v0's syntax and std require.
- Record every model gap, as the Eon studies did.
- The fixed model applies the fix commit's change and nothing else.
- The buggy model contains no bug the source lacks.
- Not portable: a candidate whose path needs more than this is "unportable", with the reason.

**Property.** It comes from the issue's own reported expected behavior. Write it in the search record, with a quote or link, before any test of that candidate runs. It is never adjusted after a run. For a hang or deadlock symptom, the property is "the trigger completes", and the simulator's deadlock or no-progress report on the faithful model counts as the property failing (as fx-zu4f.6's registered protocol defines it).

**Caught rule** (seed budget frozen at 1,000 seeds, seeds 0..999):
- the buggy model fails the property on at least one seed in the budget;
- replaying the lowest failing seed twice through the driver's recording (`tide-admit --tide-run-test … --seed N`, then `--replay`) reproduces byte-identical traces;
- the fixed model passes all 1,000 seeds.

A candidate that fails any of the three is "not caught", with the reason. Model corrections follow fx-zu4f.6's registered rule: each one cites the source lines before its rerun, corrections are counted, and any correction made after a passing full run is flagged.

## Scope
- Under `examples/case-studies/<name>/`, following eon-discovery-race and the fx-rpsb.1 runner conventions: the buggy model, with the failure declared as its expected outcome; the fixed model, passing; and a write-up. The write-up cites the issue, the fix commit and the license, gives the property with its source quote, the model and its gaps, and the seed and replay evidence. Negatives come first: what Tide does not do (it found nothing unaided; the property was supplied; the bug was already fixed upstream), and what Rust needs for the same test (loom, Shuttle, and so on; note that many of these projects already test with loom or similar tools, and say so where they do).
- A search record listing every result with its query, its eligibility outcome and reason, and, for each eligible candidate, caught, not caught or unportable, with the reason. It goes in research/ or the case study's directory.
- Report the counts: screened, eligible, caught, not caught, unportable. Present the catch as a demonstration, never as a rate.
- If several are caught, pick the shortest faithful model, breaking ties by the clearest issue and fix evidence; list the others in the record.
- If none qualifies, land the record as a documented negative and write no case study. Never stretch a candidate.

Out of scope: changes to the driver, std, runner, reference or companion; Eon and Tide bugs; posting anything upstream (outreach follows fx-zu4f's rule).

## Acceptance
- The frozen criteria above are followed, and the record lists every result with counts.
- If one is caught: `cargo test --workspace` through heavy.sh passes on the landed tree, with the buggy model's failure and the fixed model's pass as declared outcomes, and the record shows the byte-identical replay.
- If none is caught: the record lands as a documented negative, and fx-qlek.7 is told.
- GOVERNANCE.md's Merge Rule: a Codex pass, then an Opus converge round that reports instead of fixing. If Codex's cyber filter trips, an Opus stand-in reviews and the refusal is recorded.

title: Re-screen all 87 RustSec malicious-crate advisories with Proc::command and Net (new pre-registered test)
description:
## Why
fx-zu4f.5 screened every in-date RustSec advisory at advisory-db 233155b4 and found 87 reporting malicious crates. 0 were caught. The nearest miss was chrono_anchor: its buggy port gets TD0602 and TD0501, but the capability-passing version can't compile because Tide v0 had no `Proc::command`. That negative stays published as is.
Owner decision A1, 2026-11-18, relayed by tide-desk: "Bring Proc::command into the alpha, plus a network capability if the design is sound. Then Tide v0 can express the honest version of real code. Then run a fresh, pre-registered screen of all 87 malware advisories under the new rules, not only chrono_anchor." This bead is that screen. The relay authorizes it as an exception to the no-new-beads rule. It blocks the alpha RC (fx-qlek.7). Parent: fx-zu4f.
It is a NEW pre-registered test, reported as such, never as a revision of fx-zu4f.5's result.

## Frozen criteria (pre-registered by tide-lead, 2026-11-18, before the new capabilities land)
The criteria are frozen here. A builder may add operational detail in a protocol file, but must commit it and have tide-lead record its SHA-256 on this bead before ANY of these happen: the first implementation commit of fx-ayh2's Proc::command, fx-ff13 or fx-6d50 lands on main; or any port of this screen is written or run. That file may narrow the criteria; it may never widen them or change the caught rule.

**Pool, fixed: exactly these 87 advisories** (fx-zu4f.5's full screen, advisory-db 233155b4, WORK/screen-full.tsv rows with qualifies = y): RUSTSEC-2022-0042, RUSTSEC-2023-0097, RUSTSEC-2023-0098, RUSTSEC-2023-0099, RUSTSEC-2023-0100, RUSTSEC-2023-0101, RUSTSEC-2023-0102, RUSTSEC-2023-0103, RUSTSEC-2023-0104, RUSTSEC-2023-0105, RUSTSEC-2023-0106, RUSTSEC-2023-0107, RUSTSEC-2023-0108, RUSTSEC-2023-0109, RUSTSEC-2023-0110, RUSTSEC-2023-0111, RUSTSEC-2023-0112, RUSTSEC-2023-0113, RUSTSEC-2023-0114, RUSTSEC-2023-0115, RUSTSEC-2023-0116, RUSTSEC-2023-0117, RUSTSEC-2023-0118, RUSTSEC-2023-0119, RUSTSEC-2023-0120, RUSTSEC-2023-0121, RUSTSEC-2023-0122, RUSTSEC-2023-0123, RUSTSEC-2023-0124, RUSTSEC-2025-0145, RUSTSEC-2025-0146, RUSTSEC-2025-0147, RUSTSEC-2025-0148, RUSTSEC-2025-0150, RUSTSEC-2025-0151, RUSTSEC-2025-0152, RUSTSEC-2025-0154, RUSTSEC-2025-0155, RUSTSEC-2025-0156, RUSTSEC-2025-0157, RUSTSEC-2025-0158, RUSTSEC-2025-0159, RUSTSEC-2025-0160, RUSTSEC-2026-0010, RUSTSEC-2026-0011, RUSTSEC-2026-0014, RUSTSEC-2026-0015, RUSTSEC-2026-0016, RUSTSEC-2026-0017, RUSTSEC-2026-0018, RUSTSEC-2026-0019, RUSTSEC-2026-0027, RUSTSEC-2026-0028, RUSTSEC-2026-0030, RUSTSEC-2026-0031, RUSTSEC-2026-0032, RUSTSEC-2026-0036, RUSTSEC-2026-0039, RUSTSEC-2026-0040, RUSTSEC-2026-0081, RUSTSEC-2026-0084, RUSTSEC-2026-0100, RUSTSEC-2026-0102, RUSTSEC-2026-0107, RUSTSEC-2026-0108, RUSTSEC-2026-0155, RUSTSEC-2026-0171, RUSTSEC-2026-0175, RUSTSEC-2026-0259, RUSTSEC-2026-0260, RUSTSEC-2026-0261, RUSTSEC-2026-0262, RUSTSEC-2026-0264, RUSTSEC-2026-0265, RUSTSEC-2026-0266, RUSTSEC-2026-0280, RUSTSEC-2026-0281, RUSTSEC-2026-0464, RUSTSEC-2026-0465, RUSTSEC-2026-0466, RUSTSEC-2026-0467, RUSTSEC-2026-0468, RUSTSEC-2026-0469, RUSTSEC-2026-0470, RUSTSEC-2026-0471, RUSTSEC-2026-0472, RUSTSEC-2026-0483.
No advisory is added or removed. Each gets one row in the record.

**Sources.** Only the advisory text at 233155b4, reputable public write-ups that quote the affected code, and the four archive copies the owner approved for fx-zu4f.5 ("1.2"). No other crate source is fetched. An advisory with no source that quotes the affected code is "not caught (no portable source)", the same label and meaning as fx-zu4f.5.

**Capabilities.** The screen runs on one recorded main revision, after fx-ayh2's Proc::command scope has landed, along with whichever of fx-ff13 (Net::get) and fx-6d50 (Net::resolve) passed admission and the red team. The record names the revision and which capabilities it has. A port that needs a capability absent at that revision is "not caught (capability absent)", counted separately.

**Bug class.** The malicious effect, as the advisory states it: ambient process, network, filesystem, env or clock use; a detached spawn; global mutable state; or unsafe without a grant.

**Caught rule** (fx-zu4f.5's, unchanged):
- A candidate is caught when a named TD code fires on a faithful Tide port of the malicious code, and the capability-passing version, which receives the authority it uses explicitly, is admitted.
- "Faithful": port only the affected function or functions, keep their effect and structure, and change nothing beyond what Tide's syntax and std require.
- The capability-passing version changes only how the authority arrives, from ambient to a parameter. It keeps the same effect; it is not a sanitized or benign rewrite. The record shows the diff between the two versions.
- A candidate whose effect only a test or the simulator catches does not count as caught. It is "not caught" when the port is admitted, or when it would need changes beyond the faithful rule.

**Safety terms** (as in fx-zu4f.5, binding):
- All archive-derived work stays in the worktree's target/work, and the driver runs directly on files there, never under examples/.
- No payload is ever executed: admission runs only, metadata emit, no test execution of a port.
- Any network endpoint in a port points only at a simulated peer or a dead endpoint (an RFC 5737 or 6761 address).
- No malicious logic is committed. The committed record quotes only advisory text and the minimum identifiers needed.

## Scope
- A search record (research/) listing all 87 with their outcome and reason, the counts, the revision, and the capability set. Present catches as demonstrations, never as a rate.
- If any is caught: a write-up of the clearest catch for the launch materials, with the advisory, the TD codes, the trust diff of the capability-passing version, and its negatives (Tide found nothing unaided; the code was already known malicious; v0 limits). It is placed so that no malicious logic lands in the repository: ports stay in target/work and the write-up describes them.
- If none is caught: a documented negative.

Out of scope: changes to the driver, std or capabilities (fx-ayh2, fx-ff13 and fx-6d50 own those); posting anything upstream.

## Acceptance
- The protocol is registered on this bead before the capabilities' first implementation commit lands on main, and before any port. The record lists all 87 with counts.
- If any is caught: the driver output for the port and for the capability-passing version is recorded with exact commands, environment and revision, as fx-zu4f.5's r1b rerun did.
- GOVERNANCE.md's Merge Rule: a Codex pass (an Opus stand-in, recorded, if the cyber filter trips), then an Opus review round.

title: Case study: a concurrency bug from Qin et al.'s PLDI 2020 dataset found by a seeded sim_test and replayed (final pre-registered round)
description:
## Why
fx-zu4f.6 and fx-zu4f.7 found no eligible external race in GitHub searches. Most exclusions were for a missing linked fix (E1) or a path Tide v0 can't model (E4). Owner decision, 2026-11-18, relayed by tide-desk. tide-desk offered: "1 = one last pre-registered round on the published dataset from Qin et al., PLDI 2020, 'Understanding Memory and Thread Safety Practices and Issues in Real-World Rust Programs' (about 100 real concurrency bugs, blocking and non-blocking, each with its fix; a third party chose the bugs) (recommended; if it's negative, we stop and launch with the negatives); 2 = stop searching". Lucca's reply: "1". This bead is an exception to the no-new-beads rule, authorized for exactly this bead. It blocks the alpha RC (fx-qlek.7). Parent: fx-zu4f. **If this round is negative, there are no more search rounds unless Lucca asks.**

## Frozen search criteria (pre-registered by tide-lead, 2026-11-18, before any bug is examined)
The criteria are frozen here, before any search. A builder adds operational detail in a protocol file. The protocol, and the pool export below, are COMMITTED on the bead branch, and tide-lead records their SHA-256s on this bead, before any bug is examined. The protocol may narrow the criteria; it may never widen them or change the caught rule.

**Primary source** (verified by tide-lead on 2026-11-18 by read-only GET). The paper's artifact repository is github.com/system-pclub/rust-study, at commit 403b06f30809d10d2bb066d2fbcd33caf3446d17 (2020-04-17), Apache-2.0 and MIT. Its README (v1.1) says the bug list is in the Google Sheet it links (id 1GWbiPSBCIbqH2g3Vzc-o2XdxOskXyDhkJjNUjFi1pzs), in tabs "section-6.1-blocking" and "section-6.2-non-blocking", with the commit numbers in column B. The repository's section-6-thread-safety-issues/ directory holds the authors' reproductions for some bugs.

**Pool, fixed by export.** Every data row of those two tabs. The builder exports each tab once as CSV through the sheet's public export URL, records the UTC time, the URL and each file's SHA-256, and commits both files before examining any bug. No row is added or removed. If the export fails or is incomplete, the builder stops and reports BLOCKED; the paper reports 100 concurrency bugs, and the builder records the actual row counts beside it. Each row gets one record row. Duplicates (the same fix commit twice) are assessed once and cross-linked.

**Eligibility** (all must hold; record each failure's reason):
- E1: the row's fix commit (column B, or the commit or PR it names) is publicly resolvable today by read-only GET, in the named project's repository or a public mirror of it. This takes the place of fx-zu4f.6 and .7's linked-fix rule.
- E2: the symptom is stated, in the dataset row or in the fix commit, PR or linked issue. Quote it.
- E3: concurrency-shaped, as in fx-zu4f.7: a race, lost update, lost wakeup, ordering fault, deadlock or hang, or a timing-dependent flake.
- E4: the affected code path is small enough to model faithfully in Tide v0, with no network, no subprocess and no external crates. Tide's simulated Fs, Clock, tasks, channels and Shared are allowed, plus whatever Tide v0 std offers for the operations the path uses;
- E5: the bug does not depend on what Tide's simulator cannot explore. It must not need memory orderings weaker than the simulator's (a bug that appears only under Relaxed, Acquire or Release reordering is not eligible), real OS scheduling or preemption semantics beyond task interleavings at the simulator's scheduling points, or hardware or platform behavior. State each candidate's model gaps, including any atomic operation modeled as an interleaving point under sequential consistency.

- Old versions (2016-2019 code) are fine to model. State every version gap: the old std or crate API used, and how Tide v0 maps it.

**Faithful model.**
- Model only the affected code path: keep its structure, its shared state and its interleaving points (awaits, locks, channel operations, spawns). Change nothing beyond what Tide v0's syntax and std require.
- Record every model gap, as the Eon studies did.
- The fixed model applies the fix commit's change and nothing else.
- The buggy model contains no bug the source lacks.
- Not portable: a candidate whose path needs more than this is "unportable", with the reason.

**Property.** It comes from the report's own statement of the expected behavior: the dataset row, the fix commit message, the PR or the linked issue. Write it in the record with a quote or link, before any test of that candidate runs, and never adjust it after a run. For a hang or deadlock, the property is "the trigger completes", and the simulator's deadlock or no-progress report on the faithful model counts as the property failing.

**Caught rule** (seed budget frozen at 1,000 seeds, seeds 0..999; as in fx-zu4f.6 and .7):
- the buggy model fails the property on at least one seed in the budget;
- replaying the lowest failing seed twice through the driver's recording (`tide-admit --tide-run-test … --seed N`, then `--replay`) reproduces byte-identical traces;
- the fixed model passes all 1,000 seeds.
A candidate that fails any of the three is "not caught", with the reason. Model corrections follow fx-zu4f.6's registered rule: each one cites the source lines before its rerun, corrections are counted, and any correction made after a passing full run is flagged. The authors' own reproductions in section-6-thread-safety-issues/ may be read as evidence of the trigger, but the model follows the project source at the buggy revision.

## Scope
- Under `examples/case-studies/<name>/`, following eon-discovery-race and the fx-rpsb.1 runner conventions: the buggy model, with the failure declared as its expected outcome; the fixed model, passing; and a write-up. The write-up cites the issue, the fix commit and the license, gives the property with its source quote, the model and its gaps, and the seed and replay evidence. Negatives come first: what Tide does not do (it found nothing unaided; the property was supplied; the bug was already fixed upstream), and what Rust needs for the same test (loom, Shuttle, and so on, and the paper's own detectors).
- A search record listing every result with its query, its eligibility outcome and reason, and, for each eligible candidate, caught, not caught or unportable, with the reason. It goes in research/ or the case study's directory.
- Report the counts: screened, eligible, caught, not caught, unportable. Present the catch as a demonstration, never as a rate.
- If several are caught, pick the shortest faithful model, breaking ties by the clearest issue and fix evidence; list the others in the record.
- If none qualifies, land the record as a documented negative and write no case study. Never stretch a candidate.

Out of scope: changes to the driver, std, runner, reference or companion; Eon and Tide bugs; posting anything upstream (outreach follows fx-zu4f's rule).

## Acceptance
- The frozen criteria above are followed, and the record lists every result with counts.
- If one is caught: `cargo test --workspace` through heavy.sh passes on the landed tree, with the buggy model's failure and the fixed model's pass as declared outcomes, and the record shows the byte-identical replay.
- If none is caught: the record lands as a documented negative, and fx-qlek.7 is told.
- "Pre-registered" in the record means: the criteria were committed in this bead body, and the protocol and pool export were committed on the branch, before any bug was examined. It is self-attested until the repository is public (tide-desk, 2026-11-18).
- GOVERNANCE.md's Merge Rule: a Codex pass, then an Opus converge round that reports instead of fixing. If Codex's cyber filter trips, an Opus stand-in reviews and the refusal is recorded.

- The record cites Qin et al. (PLDI 2020) and the artifact, and says that the dataset's authors chose the bugs, not Tide.
